translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 124
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 124

sentences.zh: 【宋紀六】　起玄黓敦牂，盡柔兆閹茂，凡五年。

translations.literal: [Song Records 6] From Xuanyi Dunzhi through Rouzhao Yanmao; five years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Song Records 6] The span runs from Xuanyi Dunzhi through Rouzhao Yanmao—five years in all.

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝中之中元嘉十九年（

translations.literal: Middle period of Great Ancestor Emperor Wen, nineteenth year of Yuanjia (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Liu Song, nineteenth year of Yuanjia (

sentences.zh: 壬午，公元四四二年）

translations.literal: renwu, CE 442)
translations.idiomatic: renwu, CE 442)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲申，魏主備法駕，詣道壇受符菉，旗幟盡青。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, jiashen: the Northern Wei ruler, with full imperial escort, went to the Dao altar to receive talisman registers; all banners were green.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on jiashen, the Northern Wei ruler went in full imperial procession to the Dao altar to receive talisman registers; every banner was green.

sentences.zh: 自是每帝即位皆受菉。

translations.literal: From then on, every emperor upon accession received the registers.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth every new emperor received the registers upon taking the throne.

sentences.zh: 謙之又奏作靜輪宮，必令其高不聞雞犬，欲以上接天神。

translations.literal: Qianzhi again memorialized to build the Jinglun Palace, insisting it be so high that neither cock nor dog could be heard below, intending thereby to reach the celestial gods above.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi again petitioned to build the Jinglun Palace, insisting it rise so high that no cock or dog could be heard from the ground, the better to connect with the gods above.

sentences.zh: 崔浩勸帝為之，功費萬計，經年不成。

translations.literal: Cui Hao urged the emperor to undertake it; labor and expense ran into the tens of thousands, and after a full year it was still unfinished.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao urged the emperor to go ahead; the work consumed vast sums and, a year on, was still unfinished.

sentences.zh: 太子晃諫曰：「天人道殊，卑高定分，不可相接，理在必然。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Huang remonstrated, saying, "The ways of Heaven and man differ; high and low have fixed stations and cannot meet—this is necessarily so.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Huang remonstrated: "Heaven and humanity follow different paths; high and low have their allotted places and cannot meet—that is simply how things are.

sentences.zh: 今虛耗府庫，疲弊百姓，為無益之事，將安用之！

translations.literal: Now the treasury is drained empty and the people worn down, all for a useless undertaking—what use is there in it!
translations.idiomatic: Now the treasury is emptied and the people exhausted for a useless project—what good can come of it!

sentences.zh: 必如謙之所言，請因東山萬仞之高，為功差易。」

translations.literal: If it must be as Qianzhi says, please use the ten-thousand-ren height of Eastern Mountain—the work would be far easier."
translations.idiomatic: If Qianzhi's plan must be followed, use Eastern Mountain's sheer ten-thousand-ren height—the work would be far easier."

sentences.zh: 帝不從。

translations.literal: The emperor did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，沮渠無諱將萬餘家，棄敦煌西就沮渠安周。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: Juqu Wuhui led more than ten thousand households, abandoned Dunhuang, and went west to join Juqu Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Juqu Wuhui led more than ten thousand households west from Dunhuang to join Juqu Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 未至，鄯善王比龍畏之，將其眾奔且末，其世子降於安周。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, King Bilong of Shanshan, fearing him, led his people in flight to Qiemo; his heir submitted to Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before Wuhui arrived, King Bilong of Shanshan, afraid of him, fled with his people to Qiemo while his heir surrendered to Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 無諱遂據鄯善，其士卒經流沙，渴死者太半。

translations.literal: Wuhui then seized Shanshan; his soldiers crossing the shifting sands, more than half died of thirst.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhui then occupied Shanshan; crossing the shifting sands, more than half his troops died of thirst.

sentences.zh: 李寶自伊吾帥眾二千入據敦煌，繕修城府，安集故民。

translations.literal: Li Bao, from Yiwu, led two thousand men into Dunhuang, repaired the walls and fortifications, and settled the former inhabitants.
translations.idiomatic: From Yiwu, Li Bao led two thousand men into Dunhuang, repaired the walls and fortifications, and resettled the former inhabitants.

sentences.zh: 沮渠牧犍之亡也，涼州人闞爽據高昌，自稱太守。

translations.literal: When Juqu Mujian fell, Kan Shuang of Liangzhou seized Gaochang and styled himself grand administrator.
translations.idiomatic: After Juqu Mujian's fall, Kan Shuang of Liangzhou seized Gaochang and proclaimed himself grand administrator.

sentences.zh: 唐契為柔然所逼，擁眾西趨高昌，欲奪其地。

translations.literal: Tang Qi, pressed by the Rouran, gathered his followers and marched west toward Gaochang, intending to seize the territory.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed by the Rouran, Tang Qi gathered his followers and marched west on Gaochang to seize the land.

sentences.zh: 柔然遣其將阿若追擊之，契敗死。

translations.literal: The Rouran sent their general Aruo in pursuit; Qi was defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran sent General Aruo in pursuit; Qi was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 契弟和收餘眾奔車師前部王伊洛。

translations.literal: Qi's younger brother He gathered the survivors and fled to Yiluo, king of the Front Division of the Cheshi.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's younger brother He rallied the survivors and fled to Yiluo, king of the Front Division of Cheshi.

sentences.zh: 時沮渠安周屯橫截城，和攻拔之，又拔高寧、白力二城，遣使請降於魏。

translations.literal: At the time Juqu Anzhou was encamped at Hengjie City; He attacked and took it, then also took the two cities of Gaoning and Baili, and sent envoys requesting submission to Northern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Anzhou was then encamped at Hengjie City; He stormed and took it, then captured Gaoning and Baili as well, and sent envoys to submit to Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，上以疾愈，大赦。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, the emperor, his illness having healed, proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, the emperor, recovered from illness, proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 五月，裴方明等至漢中，與劉真道分兵攻武興、下辯、白水，皆取之。

translations.literal: Fifth month: Pei Fangming and others reached Hanzhong and, dividing forces with Liu Zhendao, attacked Wuxing, Xiabian, and Baishui—all were taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Pei Fangming and others reached Hanzhong; he and Liu Zhendao divided their forces and attacked Wuxing, Xiabian, and Baishui, taking them all.

sentences.zh: 楊難當遣建節將軍符弘祖守蘭皋，使其子撫軍大將軍和將重兵為後繼。

translations.literal: Yang Nandang sent Establishment of Merit General Fu Hongzu to hold Langan and had his son, General Who Pacifies the Army He, lead a heavy force as rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Nandang sent Establishment of Merit General Fu Hongzu to hold Langan and posted his son He, General Who Pacifies the Army, with a strong force in reserve.

sentences.zh: 方明與弘祖戰於濁水，大破之，斬弘祖；

translations.literal: Fangming fought Hongzu at Zhuoshui, routed him utterly, and beheaded Hongzu;
translations.idiomatic: Fangming met Hongzu at Zhuoshui, routed him, and beheaded him;

sentences.zh: 和退走，追至赤亭，又破之。

translations.literal: He retreated in flight; they pursued to Chiting and routed him again.
translations.idiomatic: He fled; they pursued to Chiting and routed him again.

sentences.zh: 難當奔上邽；

translations.literal: Nandang fled to Shanggui;
translations.idiomatic: Nandang fled to Shanggui;

sentences.zh: 獲難當兄子建節將軍保熾。

translations.literal: They captured Nandang's nephew, Establishment of Merit General Baochi.
translations.idiomatic: They captured Nandang's nephew, Establishment of Merit General Baochi.

sentences.zh: 難當以其子虎為益州刺史，守陰平，聞難當走，引兵還，至下辯；

translations.literal: Nandang had appointed his son Hu governor of Yizhou to hold Yinping; hearing that Nandang had fled, Hu led his troops back and reached Xiabian;
translations.idiomatic: Nandang had left his son Hu as governor of Yizhou to hold Yinping; hearing of his father's flight, Hu marched back and reached Xiabian;

sentences.zh: 方明使其子肅之邀擊之，擒虎，送建康，斬之；

translations.literal: Fangming had his son Suzhi intercept and attack; Hu was captured, sent to Jiankang, and beheaded;
translations.idiomatic: Fangming sent his son Suzhi to intercept him; Hu was captured, sent to Jiankang, and executed;

sentences.zh: 仇池平。

translations.literal: Qiuchi was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Qiuchi was pacified.

sentences.zh: 以輔國司馬胡崇之為北秦州刺史，鎮其地；

translations.literal: Hu Chongzhi, aide to the state, was made governor of Northern Qin and stationed to hold the territory;
translations.idiomatic: Hu Chongzhi, aide to the state, was appointed governor of Northern Qin to hold the region;

sentences.zh: 立楊保熾為楊玄後，使守仇池。

translations.literal: Yang Baochi was established as Yang Xuan's successor and set to guard Qiuchi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Baochi was installed as Yang Xuan's successor and left to guard Qiuchi.

sentences.zh: 魏人遣中山王辰迎楊難當詣平城。

translations.literal: The people of Wei sent Prince Chen of Zhongshan to welcome Yang Nandang to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei sent Prince Chen of Zhongshan to escort Yang Nandang to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，以劉真道為雍州刺史，裴方明為梁、南秦二州刺史；

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: Liu Zhendao was made governor of Yongzhou and Pei Fangming governor of the two provinces of Liang and Southern Qin;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Liu Zhendao was appointed governor of Yongzhou and Pei Fangming governor of Liang and Southern Qin;

sentences.zh: 方明辭不拜。

translations.literal: Fangming declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Fangming declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，魏主使安西將軍古弼督隴右諸軍，及殿中虎賁與武都王楊保宗自祁山南入，征西將軍漁陽皮豹子與琅邪王司馬楚之，督關中諸軍自散關西入，俱會仇池。

translations.literal: On bingyin, the Northern Wei ruler sent Pacifier of the West General Gu Bi to command the armies of Longyou, together with the Palace Tiger Guard and Prince Bao of Wudu Yang Baozong entering south from Qishan; Pacifier of the West General Pizi of Yuyang and Prince Chu of Langya Sima Chuzhi commanding the armies of Guanzhong entering west from Sanguan—all to converge on Qiuchi.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, the Northern Wei ruler sent Pacifier of the West General Gu Bi to command the Longyou armies, with the Palace Tiger Guard and Prince Bao of Wudu Yang Baozong entering south from Qishan, while Pacifier of the West General Pizi of Yuyang and Prince Chu of Langya Sima Chuzhi led the Guanzhong armies in from Sanguan—all converging on Qiuchi.

sentences.zh: 又使譙王司馬文思督洛、豫諸軍南趨襄陽，征南將軍刁雍東趨廣陵，移書徐州，稱為楊難當報仇。

translations.literal: He also sent Prince Wen of Qiao Sima Wensi to command the armies of Luoyang and Yuzhou south toward Xiangyang, and Pacifier of the South General Diao Yong east toward Guangling, sending a letter to Xuzhou claiming to avenge Yang Nandang.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Prince Wen of Qiao Sima Wensi to lead the Luoyang and Yuzhou armies south on Xiangyang, and Pacifier of the South General Diao Yong east on Guangling, writing to Xuzhou that he came to avenge Yang Nandang.

sentences.zh: 甲戌晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: On the last day of jiaxu, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of jiaxu, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 唐契之攻闞爽也，爽遣使詐降於沮渠無諱，欲與之共擊契。

translations.literal: When Tang Qi attacked Kan Shuang, Shuang sent envoys feigning submission to Juqu Wuhui, intending to join with him in attacking Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang Qi attacked Kan Shuang, Shuang sent envoys feigning surrender to Juqu Wuhui, hoping to join forces against Qi.

sentences.zh: 八月，無諱將其眾趨高昌；

translations.literal: Eighth month: Wuhui led his followers toward Gaochang;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Wuhui marched on Gaochang;

sentences.zh: 比至，契已死，爽閉門拒之。

translations.literal: By the time he arrived, Qi was already dead; Shuang shut the gates and refused him.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he arrived, Qi was dead; Shuang shut the gates against him.

sentences.zh: 九月，無諱將衛興奴夜襲高昌，屠其城，爽奔柔然。

translations.literal: Ninth month: Wuhui's general Wei Xingnu raided Gaochang by night, slaughtered the city, and Shuang fled to the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Wuhui's general Wei Xingnu stormed Gaochang by night, sacked the city, and Shuang fled to the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 無諱據高昌，遣其常侍汜俊奉表詣建康。

translations.literal: Wuhui seized Gaochang and sent his regular attendant Si Jun bearing a memorial to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhui occupied Gaochang and sent his regular attendant Si Jun with a memorial to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 詔以無諱為都督涼、河、沙三州諸軍事、征西大將軍、涼州刺史、河西王。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Wuhui area commander of military affairs for the three provinces of Liang, He, and Sha, Grand General Who Pacifies the West, governor of Liangzhou, and Prince of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Wuhui area commander for Liang, He, and Sha, Grand General Who Pacifies the West, governor of Liangzhou, and Prince of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己卯，魏立皇子伏羅為晉王，翰為秦王，譚為燕王，建為楚王，余為吳王。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, on jimao: Northern Wei enfeoffed the princes—Fula as Prince of Jin, Han as Prince of Qin, Tan as Prince of Yan, Jian as Prince of Chu, and Yu as Prince of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jimao, Northern Wei enfeoffed the princes: Fula as Prince of Jin, Han as Prince of Qin, Tan as Prince of Yan, Jian as Prince of Chu, and Yu as Prince of Wu.

sentences.zh: 甲申，柔然遣使詣建康。

translations.literal: On jiashen, the Rouran sent envoys to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, the Rouran sent envoys to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 十二月，辛已，魏襄城孝王盧魯元卒。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on xinsi: Prince Xia of Xiangcheng, Lu Luyuan of Northern Wei, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on xinsi, Prince Xia of Xiangcheng, Lu Luyuan of Northern Wei, died.

sentences.zh: 丙申，詔魯郡修孔子廟及學舍，蠲墓側五戶課役以供灑掃。

translations.literal: On bingshen, an edict ordered Lu Commandery to repair the temple of Confucius and the academy, and exempted five households beside the tomb from corvée to provide for sweeping and cleaning.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, an edict ordered Lu Commandery to restore Confucius's temple and the academy, and exempted five households beside the tomb from corvée to maintain the grounds.

sentences.zh: 李寶遣其弟懷達、子承奉表詣平城；

translations.literal: Li Bao sent his younger brother Huaida and his son Cheng bearing a memorial to Pingcheng;
translations.idiomatic: Li Bao sent his brother Huaida and his son Cheng with a memorial to Pingcheng;

sentences.zh: 魏人以寶為都督西垂諸軍事、鎮西大將軍、開府儀同三司、沙州牧、敦煌公，四品以下聽承製假授。

translations.literal: The people of Wei made Bao area commander of military affairs for the western frontier, Grand General Who Guards the West, grand master with honors equal to the Three Excellencies, governor of Shazhou, and Duke of Dunhuang, with authority to provisionally appoint officials of fourth rank and below.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei appointed Bao area commander of the western frontier, Grand General Who Guards the West, grand master with honors equal to the Three Excellencies, governor of Shazhou, and Duke of Dunhuang, with authority to provisionally appoint officials of fourth rank and below.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史晉安襄侯劉道產卒。

translations.literal: Marquis Xiang of Jin'an, Liu Daochan, governor of Yongzhou, died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daochan, Marquis Xiang of Jin'an and governor of Yongzhou, died.

sentences.zh: 道產善為政，民安其業，小大豐贍，由是民間有《襄陽樂歌》。

translations.literal: Daochan governed well; the people were secure in their occupations, great and small alike were abundantly provided for, and hence among the people there arose the "Xiangyang Songs of Joy."
translations.idiomatic: Daochan governed well; the people were secure in their trades, all prospered, and the people composed the "Xiangyang Songs of Joy."

sentences.zh: 山蠻前後不可制者皆出，緣沔為村落，戶口殷盛。

translations.literal: Mountain tribesmen who before and after had been uncontrollable all came forth, settled along the Han as villages, and their population flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain tribesmen who had long defied control came out and settled in villages along the Han; their numbers swelled.

sentences.zh: 及卒，蠻追送至沔口。

translations.literal: When he died, the tribesmen followed in mourning to the mouth of the Han.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, the tribesmen followed his funeral procession to the mouth of the Han.

sentences.zh: 未幾，群蠻大動，征西司馬朱修之討之，不利；

translations.literal: Before long, the tribes rose in great numbers; Pacifier of the West aide Zhu Xiuzhi campaigned against them without success;
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, the tribes rose in force; Pacifier of the West aide Zhu Xiuzhi campaigned against them without success;

sentences.zh: 詔建威將軍沈慶之代之，殺虜萬餘人。

translations.literal: An edict replaced him with General Who Establishes Might Shen Qingzhi, who killed more than ten thousand of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent General Who Establishes Might Shen Qingzhi to replace him; he killed more than ten thousand of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 魏主使尚書李順差次群臣，賜以爵位；

translations.literal: The Northern Wei ruler had Minister of the Interior Li Shun rank the ministers in order and bestow titles of nobility;
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei ruler had Minister of the Interior Li Shun rank the ministers and bestow titles of nobility;

sentences.zh: 順受賄，品第不平。

translations.literal: Shun accepted bribes and the rankings were unfair.
translations.idiomatic: Shun took bribes and the rankings were unjust.

sentences.zh: 是歲，涼州人徐桀告之，魏主怒，且以順保庇沮渠氏，面欺誤國，賜順死。

translations.literal: That year, Xu Jie of Liangzhou reported him; the Northern Wei ruler was enraged, and moreover because Shun had shielded the Juqu clan and deceived the ruler to the nation's harm, he was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: That year Xu Jie of Liangzhou reported him; the Northern Wei ruler was furious, and because Shun had shielded the Juqu clan and deceived the throne to the nation's harm, he was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝中之中元嘉二十年（

translations.literal: Middle period of Great Ancestor Emperor Wen, twentieth year of Yuanjia (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Liu Song, twentieth year of Yuanjia (

sentences.zh: 癸未，公元四四三年）

translations.literal: guiwei, CE 443)
translations.idiomatic: guiwei, CE 443)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，魏皮豹子等進擊樂鄉，將軍王奐之等敗沒。

translations.literal: Spring, first month: Northern Wei's Pizi and others advanced to attack Leyang; Generals Wang Huanzhi and others were defeated and perished.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Northern Wei's Pizi and others advanced on Leyang; Generals Wang Huanzhi and others were defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 魏軍進至下辯，將軍強玄明等敗死。

translations.literal: The Wei army advanced to Xiabian; Generals Qiang Xuanming and others were defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei army pushed on to Xiabian; Generals Qiang Xuanming and others were defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 二月，胡崇之與魏戰於濁水，崇之為魏所擒，餘眾走還漢中。

translations.literal: Second month: Hu Chongzhi fought Wei at Zhuoshui; Chongzhi was captured by Wei and the survivors fled back to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Hu Chongzhi fought Northern Wei at Zhuoshui; Chongzhi was captured and the survivors fled back to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 將軍姜道祖兵敗，降魏，魏遂取仇池。

translations.literal: General Jiang Daozu was defeated, surrendered to Wei, and Wei then took Qiuchi.
translations.idiomatic: General Jiang Daozu was defeated, surrendered to Northern Wei, and Northern Wei then took Qiuchi.

sentences.zh: 楊保熾走。

translations.literal: Yang Baochi fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Baochi fled.

sentences.zh: 丙午，魏主如恆山之陽；

translations.literal: On bingwu, the Northern Wei ruler went to the southern face of Mount Heng;
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, the Northern Wei ruler went to the southern face of Mount Heng;

sentences.zh: 三月，庚申，還宮。

translations.literal: Third month, on gengshen, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on gengshen, he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，烏洛侯國遣使如魏。

translations.literal: On renxu, the state of Wuluohou sent envoys to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, the state of Wuluohou sent envoys to Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 初，魏之居北荒也，鑿石為廟，在烏洛侯西北，以祀其先，高七十尺，深九十步。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wei dwelt in the northern wilds, they carved stone into a shrine northwest of Wuluohou to sacrifice to their ancestors—seventy feet high and ninety paces deep.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago, when Northern Wei still lived in the northern wilds, they carved a stone shrine northwest of Wuluohou to honor their ancestors—seventy feet high and ninety paces deep.

sentences.zh: 及烏洛侯使者至魏，言石廟具在，魏主遣中書侍郎李敞詣石廟致祭，刻祝文於壁而還，去平城四千餘里。

translations.literal: When the Wuluohou envoys reached Wei and reported that the stone shrine still stood intact, the Northern Wei ruler sent Secretariat Gentleman Li Chang to the stone shrine to perform sacrifice, carved a prayer text on the wall, and returned—more than four thousand li from Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wuluohou envoys reached Northern Wei and reported the stone shrine still intact, the Northern Wei ruler sent Secretariat Gentleman Li Chang to sacrifice there, carved a prayer on the wall, and returned—more than four thousand li from Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 魏河間公齊與武都王楊保宗對鎮雒谷，保宗弟文德說保宗，令閉險自固以叛魏。

translations.literal: Duke Qi of Hejian of Wei and Prince Bao of Wudu Yang Baozong were stationed opposite each other at Luogu; Baozong's younger brother Wendé persuaded Baozong to shut the passes, hold himself secure, and rebel against Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Qi of Hejian of Northern Wei and Prince Bao of Wudu Yang Baozong faced each other at Luogu; Baozong's brother Wendé urged him to seal the passes, hold fast, and rebel against Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 或以告齊，夏，四月，齊誘執保宗，送平城，殺之。

translations.literal: Someone reported this to Qi; summer, fourth month: Qi lured and seized Baozong, sent him to Pingcheng, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Someone informed Qi; in summer, the fourth month, Qi lured Baozong into custody, sent him to Pingcheng, and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 前鎮東司符達、征西從事中郎任朏等遂舉兵立楊文德為主，據白崖，分兵取諸戍，進圍仇池，自號征西將軍、秦、河、梁三州牧、仇池公。

translations.literal: Former Pacifier of the East aide Fu Da, Pacifier of the West attendant Ren Fei, and others then raised troops, established Yang Wendé as leader, seized Baiya, divided forces to take the garrisons, advanced to besiege Qiuchi, and styled themselves General Who Pacifies the West, governor of the three provinces of Qin, He, and Liang, and Duke of Qiuchi.
translations.idiomatic: Former Pacifier of the East aide Fu Da, Pacifier of the West attendant Ren Fei, and others then raised troops, installed Yang Wendé as leader, seized Baiya, took the garrisons, and besieged Qiuchi, styling Wendé General Who Pacifies the West, governor of Qin, He, and Liang, and Duke of Qiuchi.

sentences.zh: 甲午，立皇子誕為廣陵王。

translations.literal: On jiawu, the prince Dan was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Prince Dan was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，魏大赦。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Northern Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Northern Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 己亥，魏主如陰山。

translations.literal: On jihai, the Northern Wei ruler went to the Yin Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, the Northern Wei ruler went to the Yin Mountains.

sentences.zh: 五月，魏古弼發上邽、高平、岍城諸軍擊楊文德，文德退走。

translations.literal: Fifth month: Northern Wei's Gu Bi mobilized the armies of Shanggui, Gaoping, and Qiancheng to attack Yang Wendé; Wendé retreated in flight.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Northern Wei's Gu Bi mobilized the armies of Shanggui, Gaoping, and Qiancheng against Yang Wendé; Wendé retreated.

sentences.zh: 皮豹子督關中諸軍至下辯，聞仇池解圍，欲還；

translations.literal: Pizi, commanding the armies of Guanzhong, reached Xiabian; hearing that the siege of Qiuchi was lifted, he wished to return;
translations.idiomatic: Pizi, commanding the Guanzhong armies, reached Xiabian; hearing the siege of Qiuchi was lifted, he wanted to withdraw;

sentences.zh: 弼遣人謂豹子曰：「宋人恥敗，必將復來。

translations.literal: Bi sent someone to tell Pizi, "The Song are shamed by defeat and will surely come again.
translations.idiomatic: Bi sent word to Pizi: "The Song are shamed by defeat and will surely return.

sentences.zh: 軍還之後，再舉為難，不如練兵蓄力以待之。

translations.literal: After the army withdraws, they will raise trouble again—it is better to drill the troops and store up strength to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Once you withdraw, they will trouble us again; better to drill the troops and gather strength and wait.

sentences.zh: 不出秋冬，宋師必至；

translations.literal: Before autumn and winter are out, Song forces will surely arrive;
translations.idiomatic: Before autumn and winter are out, Song forces will come;

sentences.zh: 以逸待勞，無不克矣。」

translations.literal: To await the weary with rested troops—nothing will fail to be overcome."
translations.idiomatic: Meet their weariness with rested troops, and you cannot fail."

sentences.zh: 豹子從之。

translations.literal: Pizi complied.
translations.idiomatic: Pizi agreed.

sentences.zh: 魏以豹子為仇池鎮將。

translations.literal: Wei made Pizi garrison commander of Qiuchi.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei made Pizi garrison commander of Qiuchi.

sentences.zh: 楊文德遣使來求援。

translations.literal: Yang Wendé sent envoys to request aid.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wendé sent envoys asking for help.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸丑，詔以文德為都督北秦、雍二州諸軍事、征西大將軍、北秦州刺史、武都王。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, on guichou: an edict made Wendé area commander of military affairs for the two provinces of Northern Qin and Yong, Grand General Who Pacifies the West, governor of Northern Qin, and Prince of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on guichou, an edict made Wendé area commander of Northern Qin and Yong, Grand General Who Pacifies the West, governor of Northern Qin, and Prince of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 文德屯葭蘆城，以任朏為左司馬；

translations.literal: Wendé encamped at Jialu City and made Ren Fei left aide;
translations.idiomatic: Wendé encamped at Jialu City and made Ren Fei his left aide;

sentences.zh: 武都、陰平氐多歸之。

translations.literal: Many of the Di of Wudu and Yinping submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Many Di of Wudu and Yinping rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 甲子，前雍州刺史劉真道、梁、南秦二州刺史裴方明，坐破仇池減匿金寶及善馬，下獄死。

translations.literal: On jiazi, former governor of Yongzhou Liu Zhendao and governor of the two provinces of Liang and Southern Qin Pei Fangming, for having concealed gold, jewels, and fine horses after the conquest of Qiuchi, were imprisoned and died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, former governor of Yongzhou Liu Zhendao and governor of Liang and Southern Qin Pei Fangming, convicted of concealing gold, jewels, and fine horses after the conquest of Qiuchi, were imprisoned and executed.

sentences.zh: 九月，辛巳，魏主如漠南。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on xinsi: the Northern Wei ruler went to the region south of the desert.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on xinsi, the Northern Wei ruler went south of the desert.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，捨輜重，以輕騎襲柔然。

translations.literal: On jiachen, abandoning baggage trains, he raided the Rouran with light cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, leaving the baggage train behind, he struck the Rouran with light cavalry.

sentences.zh: 分軍為四道：樂安王范、建寧王崇各統十五將出東道，樂平王丕督十五將出西道，魏主出中道，中山王辰督十五將為後繼。

translations.literal: The army was divided into four routes: Prince Fan of Le'an and Prince Chong of Jianning each commanded fifteen generals on the eastern route; Prince Pi of Leping supervised fifteen generals on the western route; the Northern Wei ruler took the central route; and Prince Chen of Zhongshan supervised fifteen generals as rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: He divided the army into four columns: Prince Fan of Le'an and Prince Chong of Jianning each led fifteen generals on the eastern route; Prince Pi of Leping led fifteen generals on the western route; the Northern Wei ruler took the center; and Prince Chen of Zhongshan led fifteen generals in reserve.

sentences.zh: 魏主至鹿渾谷，遇敕連可汗。

translations.literal: The Northern Wei ruler reached Luhun Valley and encountered Khan Chelian.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei ruler reached Luhun Valley and encountered Khan Chelian.

sentences.zh: 太子晃言於魏主曰：「賊不意大軍猝至，宜掩其不備，速進擊之。」

translations.literal: Crown Prince Huang said to the Northern Wei ruler, "The enemy did not expect the great army to arrive so suddenly; we should take them unawares and strike quickly."
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Huang said to the Northern Wei ruler, "The enemy did not expect our main force so soon; we should take them by surprise and strike at once."

sentences.zh: 尚書令劉絜固諫，以為賊營中塵盛，其眾必多，出至平地，恐為所圍。

translations.literal: Minister of the Interior Liu Jie firmly remonstrated, holding that dust was thick in the enemy camp and their numbers must be great; if they went out onto open ground, they feared being surrounded.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the Interior Liu Jie firmly objected, arguing that dust hung thick over the enemy camp and their numbers must be great; on open ground they risked encirclement.

sentences.zh: 不如須諸軍大集，然後擊之。

translations.literal: It would be better to wait until the armies had fully assembled, then attack.
translations.idiomatic: Better to wait until all the armies had gathered, then attack.

sentences.zh: 晃曰：「塵之盛者，由軍士驚怖擾亂故也，何得營上而有此塵乎！」

translations.literal: Huang said, "When dust is thick, it is because the soldiers are panicked and in disorder—how could there be such dust above the camp!"
translations.idiomatic: Huang said, "Thick dust means panicked, disorderly troops—how could dust like that hang over their camp!"

sentences.zh: 魏主疑之，不急擊。

translations.literal: The Northern Wei ruler was doubtful and did not press the attack.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei ruler hesitated and did not press the attack.

sentences.zh: 柔然遁去。

translations.literal: The Rouran fled away.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran fled.

sentences.zh: 追至石水，不及而還。

translations.literal: They pursued to Shishui, failed to overtake them, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They pursued as far as Shishui, failed to catch them, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 既而獲柔然候騎曰：「柔然不覺魏軍至，上下惶駭，引眾北走，經六七日，知無追者，始乃徐行。」

translations.literal: Later they captured a Rouran scout who said, "The Rouran did not realize the Wei army had arrived; high and low were panic-stricken and led their followers north in flight. After six or seven days, knowing there were no pursuers, they only then proceeded at leisure."
translations.idiomatic: Later they captured a Rouran scout who said, "The Rouran never noticed the Northern Wei army's arrival; the whole camp panicked and fled north. After six or seven days, seeing no pursuit, they slowed to an easy march."

sentences.zh: 魏主深恨之。

translations.literal: The Northern Wei ruler deeply resented this.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei ruler deeply resented it.

sentences.zh: 自是軍國大事，皆與太子謀之。

translations.literal: From then on, all great affairs of army and state were deliberated with the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth all major military and state affairs were discussed with the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 司馬楚之別將兵督軍糧，鎮北將軍封沓亡降柔然，說柔然令擊楚之以絕軍食。

translations.literal: Sima Chuzhi, on detached duty, commanded troops supervising army grain; General Who Guards the North Feng Ta defected to the Rouran and urged them to attack Chuzhi to cut off the army's food supply.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Chuzhi, on detached duty, supervised army grain; General Who Guards the North Feng Ta defected to the Rouran and urged them to strike Chuzhi and cut off the army's supplies.

sentences.zh: 俄而軍中有告失驢耳者，諸將莫曉其故。

translations.literal: Soon someone in the army reported missing donkey ears, and none of the generals understood the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Soon someone reported missing donkey ears in camp, and none of the generals understood why.

sentences.zh: 楚之曰：「此必賊遣奸人入營覘伺，割驢耳以為信耳。

translations.literal: Chuzhi said, "This must mean the enemy sent spies into camp to reconnoiter and cut donkey ears as proof.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhi said, "The enemy must have sent spies into camp and cut donkey ears as proof of their reconnaissance.

sentences.zh: 賊至不久，宜急為之備。」

translations.literal: The enemy will arrive before long; we should prepare at once."
translations.idiomatic: They will strike soon—we must prepare at once."

sentences.zh: 乃伐仰為城，以水灌之，令凍；

translations.literal: They then felled trees upright to make a wall, poured water over it, and let it freeze;
translations.idiomatic: They felled trees upright for a wall, flooded it with water, and let it freeze;

sentences.zh: 城立而柔然至，冰堅滑，不可攻，乃散走。

translations.literal: the wall stood and the Rouran arrived; the ice was hard and slick and could not be assaulted, and they dispersed and fled.
translations.idiomatic: the wall was ready when the Rouran arrived; the ice was hard and slick, they could not attack, and they scattered.

sentences.zh: 十一月，將軍姜道盛與楊文德合眾二萬攻魏濁水戍，魏皮豹子、河間公齊救之，道盛敗死。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: General Jiang Daosheng joined Yang Wendé with twenty thousand men to attack the Wei garrison at Zhuoshui; Northern Wei's Pizi and Duke Qi of Hejian came to the rescue, and Daosheng was defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, General Jiang Daosheng and Yang Wendé combined twenty thousand men to attack the Northern Wei garrison at Zhuoshui; Pizi and Duke Qi of Hejian rescued it, and Daosheng was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 甲子，魏主還，至朔方，下詔令皇太子副理萬機，總統百揆。

translations.literal: On jiazi, the Northern Wei ruler returned and reached Shuofang; he issued an edict ordering the crown prince to assist in governing all affairs and to preside over the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, the Northern Wei ruler returned to Shuofang and ordered the crown prince to assist in governing all affairs and preside over the hundred officials.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「諸功臣勤勞日久，皆當以爵歸第，隨時朝請，饗宴朕前，論道陳謨而已，不宜復煩以劇職；

translations.literal: He also said, "The meritorious ministers have toiled long; all should retire to their estates with their titles, attend court as occasion requires, feast before me, and discuss the Way and offer counsel—that is all; they should not again be burdened with heavy duties;
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "The meritorious ministers have toiled long; all should retire to their estates with their titles, attend court when required, feast before me, and discuss policy—that is enough; they should not again be burdened with heavy duties;

sentences.zh: 更舉賢俊以備百官。」

translations.literal: select worthy and talented men anew to fill the hundred offices."
translations.idiomatic: select worthy men anew to fill the hundred offices."

sentences.zh: 十二月，辛卯，魏主還平城。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on xinmao: the Northern Wei ruler returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on xinmao, the Northern Wei ruler returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝中之中元嘉二十一年（

translations.literal: Middle period of Great Ancestor Emperor Wen, twenty-first year of Yuanjia (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Liu Song, twenty-first year of Yuanjia (

sentences.zh: 甲申，公元四四四年）

translations.literal: jiashen, CE 444)
translations.idiomatic: jiashen, CE 444)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己亥，帝耕藉田，大赦。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on jihai: the emperor plowed the sacred field and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on jihai, the emperor plowed the sacred field and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，魏太子始總百揆，命侍中、中書監穆壽、司徒崔浩、侍中張黎、古弼輔太子決庶政，上書者皆稱臣，儀與表同。

translations.literal: On renyin, the Northern Wei crown prince began to preside over the hundred officials; he appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Secretariat Mu Shou, Minister of Education Cui Hao, Attendant-in-Ordinary Zhang Li, and Gu Bi to assist the crown prince in deciding ordinary affairs; all who submitted memorials addressed themselves as subjects, with ceremony the same as for formal petitions.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, the Northern Wei crown prince began presiding over the hundred officials; he appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Secretariat Mu Shou, Minister of Education Cui Hao, Attendant-in-Ordinary Zhang Li, and Gu Bi to assist him in ordinary governance; all memorialists addressed themselves as subjects, with ceremony matching formal petitions.

sentences.zh: 古弼為人，忠慎質直。

translations.literal: Gu Bi as a man was loyal, cautious, plain, and upright.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Bi was loyal, cautious, plain, and upright.

sentences.zh: 嘗以上谷苑囿太廣，乞減太半以賜貧民，入見魏主，欲奏其事。

translations.literal: Once, because the Shanggu park and preserves were too vast, he petitioned to reduce them by more than half and grant the land to the poor; he entered to see the Northern Wei ruler intending to report the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Once, finding the Shanggu park and preserves too vast, he petitioned to cut them by more than half for the poor; he came before the Northern Wei ruler to report it.

sentences.zh: 帝方與給事中劉樹圍棋，志不在弼。

translations.literal: The emperor was just playing go with Supervising Secretary Liu Shu; his mind was not on Bi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was playing go with Supervising Secretary Liu Shu and paid Bi no mind.

sentences.zh: 弼侍坐良久，不獲陳聞。

translations.literal: Bi sat in attendance a long time without being able to state his report.
translations.idiomatic: Bi waited in attendance a long time without being heard.

sentences.zh: 忽起，手卒樹頭，掣下床，搏其耳，毆其背，曰：「朝廷不治，實爾之罪！」

translations.literal: Suddenly he rose, seized Shu by the head, dragged him from the couch, boxed his ears and beat his back, saying, "The court is ill-governed—the fault is truly yours!"
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly he rose, grabbed Shu by the head, dragged him from the couch, boxed his ears and beat his back, crying, "The court is ill-governed—and the fault is yours!"

sentences.zh: 帝失容，捨棋曰：「不聽奏事，朕之過也，樹何罪！

translations.literal: The emperor lost composure, set aside the go stones, and said, "Not hearing reports is my fault—what crime has Shu!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flushed, set the stones aside, and said, "Not hearing reports is my fault—what has Shu done wrong!

sentences.zh: 置之！」

translations.literal: Release him!"
translations.idiomatic: Let him go!"

sentences.zh: 弼具以狀聞，帝皆可其奏。

translations.literal: Bi fully reported the matter, and the emperor approved all his petition.
translations.idiomatic: Bi then reported the matter in full, and the emperor approved it all.

sentences.zh: 弼曰：「為人臣無禮至此，其罪大矣！」

translations.literal: Bi said, "For a subject to be so lacking in propriety—the crime is great!"
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "For a subject to behave so— the offense is grave!"

sentences.zh: 出詣公車，免冠徒跣請罪。

translations.literal: He went out to the imperial carriage office, removed cap and shoes, and begged punishment barefoot.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the imperial carriage office, removed cap and shoes, and begged punishment barefoot.

sentences.zh: 帝召入，謂曰：「吾聞築社之役，蹇蹶而築之，端冕而事之，神降之福。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him in and said, "I have heard that in building an altar to the soil god, one builds though lame and crippled, and serves it in full regalia, and the spirits bestow blessing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him and said, "I have heard that in building an altar to the soil god, one builds though lame and crippled, serves in full regalia, and the spirits bestow blessing.

sentences.zh: 然則卿有何罪！

translations.literal: Then what crime have you!
translations.idiomatic: What crime have you, then!

sentences.zh: 其冠履就職。

translations.literal: Put on cap and shoes and resume your post.
translations.idiomatic: Put on cap and shoes and resume your post.

sentences.zh: 苟有可以利社稷、便百姓者，竭力為之，勿顧慮也。」

translations.literal: If there is anything that can benefit the altars of soil and grain and ease the people, do it with all your strength and do not hold back."
translations.idiomatic: Whatever can benefit the state and ease the people, do it with all your strength and do not hold back."

sentences.zh: 太子課民稼穡，使無牛者借人牛以耕種，而為之芸田以償之，凡耕種二十二畝而芸七畝，大略以是為率。

translations.literal: The crown prince assessed the people's farming: those without oxen borrowed others' oxen to plow and sow, and weeded fields in repayment; for every twenty-two mu plowed and sown, seven mu were weeded—roughly this was the rate.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince assessed farming: those without oxen borrowed others' oxen to plow and sow, then weeded fields in repayment—roughly seven mu weeded for every twenty-two mu plowed.

sentences.zh: 使民各標姓名於田首，以知其勤惰，禁飲酒遊戲者。

translations.literal: He had the people each mark their names at the head of the field to show diligence or sloth, and forbade drinking and gaming.
translations.idiomatic: He had each farmer mark his name at the field's edge to show diligence or sloth, and forbade drinking and gaming.

sentences.zh: 於是墾田大增。

translations.literal: Thereupon newly opened fields greatly increased.
translations.idiomatic: Newly opened fields increased greatly.

sentences.zh: 戊申，魏主詔：「王、公以下至庶人，有私養沙門、巫覡於家者，皆遣詣官曹；

translations.literal: On wushen, the Northern Wei ruler decreed, "From kings and dukes down to commoners, whoever privately keeps Buddhist monks or shamans at home must send them to the official offices;
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, the Northern Wei ruler decreed, "From kings and dukes down to commoners, anyone keeping Buddhist monks or shamans at home must send them to the official offices;

sentences.zh: 過二月十五日不出，沙門、巫覡死，主人門誅。」

translations.literal: if after the fifteenth of the second month they have not come forth, the monks and shamans die and the household is punished by execution to the gate."
translations.idiomatic: if after the fifteenth of the second month they have not come forth, the monks and shamans die and the household is executed to the gate."

sentences.zh: 庚戌，又詔：「王、公、卿、大夫之子皆詣太學，其百工、商賈之子，當各習父兄之業，毋得私立學校；

translations.literal: On gengxu, he decreed again, "The sons of kings, dukes, ministers, and grand masters must all attend the Imperial Academy; the sons of artisans and merchants must each practice their fathers' and elder brothers' trades and may not privately establish schools;
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, he decreed again, "The sons of kings, dukes, ministers, and grand masters must attend the Imperial Academy; the sons of artisans and merchants must each follow their fathers' and elder brothers' trades and may not privately establish schools;

sentences.zh: 違者，師死，主人門誅。」

translations.literal: violators: the teacher dies and the household is punished by execution to the gate."
translations.idiomatic: violators: the teacher dies and the household is executed to the gate."

sentences.zh: 二月，辛未，魏中山王辰、內都坐大官薛辨、尚書奚眷等八將坐擊柔然後期，斬於都南。

translations.literal: Second month, on xinwei: Northern Wei's Prince Chen of Zhongshan, Chief Palace Provisioner Xue Bian, Minister Xi Juan, and eight other generals were beheaded south of the capital for arriving late in the attack on the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on xinwei, Northern Wei's Prince Chen of Zhongshan, Chief Palace Provisioner Xue Bian, Minister Xi Juan, and eight other generals were beheaded south of the capital for arriving late against the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 初，魏尚書令劉絜，久典機要，恃寵自專，魏主心惡之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Northern Wei's Minister of the Interior Liu Jie had long held control of vital affairs, relied on favor and acted on his own authority, and the Northern Wei ruler inwardly hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Northern Wei's Minister of the Interior Liu Jie had long controlled vital affairs, relied on favor and acted arbitrarily, and the Northern Wei ruler inwardly hated him.

sentences.zh: 及將襲柔然，絜諫曰：「蠕蠕遷徙無常，前者出師，勞而無功；

translations.literal: When about to raid the Rouran, Jie remonstrated, "The Ruru move without fixed abode; the previous campaign was toilsome and fruitless;
translations.idiomatic: When about to raid the Rouran, Jie remonstrated, "The Ruru roam without fixed abode; the last campaign was toilsome and fruitless;

sentences.zh: 不如廣農積穀以待其來。」

translations.literal: it would be better to expand farming and store grain to await their coming."
translations.idiomatic: better to expand farming and store grain and wait for them to come."

sentences.zh: 崔浩固勸魏主行，魏主從之。

translations.literal: Cui Hao firmly urged the Northern Wei ruler to go, and the Northern Wei ruler complied.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao firmly urged the Northern Wei ruler to go, and he agreed.

sentences.zh: 絜恥其言不用，欲敗魏師；

translations.literal: Jie was shamed that his words were not heeded and wished to ruin the Wei army;
translations.idiomatic: Jie was shamed that his advice was ignored and sought to ruin the Northern Wei army;

sentences.zh: 魏主與諸將期會鹿渾谷，絜矯詔易其期。

translations.literal: the Northern Wei ruler had fixed a rendezvous with the generals at Luhun Valley, and Jie forged an edict changing the date.
translations.idiomatic: the Northern Wei ruler had fixed a rendezvous with his generals at Luhun Valley, and Jie forged an edict changing the date.

sentences.zh: 帝至鹿渾谷，欲擊柔然，絜諫止之，使待諸將。

translations.literal: The emperor reached Luhun Valley and wished to attack the Rouran; Jie remonstrated and stopped him, making him wait for the generals.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reached Luhun Valley and wished to attack the Rouran; Jie remonstrated and stopped him, making him wait for the generals.

sentences.zh: 帝留鹿渾谷六日，諸將不至，柔然遂遠遁，追之不及。

translations.literal: The emperor remained at Luhun Valley six days; the generals did not arrive; the Rouran then fled far away and could not be overtaken in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor waited at Luhun Valley six days; the generals never came; the Rouran fled far away and could not be caught.

sentences.zh: 軍還，經漠中，糧盡，士卒多死。

translations.literal: The army returned, crossing the desert; grain was exhausted and many soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: Returning through the desert, grain ran out and many soldiers died.

sentences.zh: 絜陰使人驚魏軍，勸帝委軍輕還，帝不從。

translations.literal: Jie secretly had people alarm the Wei army and urged the emperor to abandon the army and return lightly; the emperor did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Jie secretly spread alarm in the army and urged the emperor to abandon the troops and return lightly; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 絜以軍出無功，請治崔浩之罪。

translations.literal: Jie, because the campaign had achieved nothing, requested that Cui Hao be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Jie, because the campaign had failed, demanded that Cui Hao be punished.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「諸將失期，遇賊不擊，浩何罪也！」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "The generals missed the rendezvous and did not strike when they met the enemy—what crime has Hao!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The generals missed the rendezvous and failed to strike—what crime has Hao committed!"

sentences.zh: 浩以絜矯詔事白帝，帝至五原，收絜，囚之。

translations.literal: Hao reported to the emperor Jie's forgery of the edict; the emperor reached Wuyuan, seized Jie, and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Hao reported Jie's forgery to the emperor; at Wuyuan the emperor seized Jie and imprisoned him.

sentences.zh: 帝之北行也，絜私謂所親曰：「若車駕不返，吾當立樂平王。」

translations.literal: When the emperor marched north, Jie privately told those close to him, "If the imperial carriage does not return, I shall establish the Prince of Leping."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched north, Jie privately told confidants, "If the emperor does not return, I shall establish the Prince of Leping."

sentences.zh: 絜聞尚書右丞張嵩家有圖讖，問曰：「劉氏應王，繼國家後，吾有姓名否？

translations.literal: Jie heard that Vice Director of the Secretariat Zhang Song's household possessed prognostic charts and asked, "The Liu clan is destined to rule and succeed the state—do I have name or surname therein?
translations.idiomatic: Jie heard that Vice Director of the Secretariat Zhang Song possessed prognostic charts and asked, "The Liu clan is destined to rule and succeed the state—is my name among them?

sentences.zh: 嵩曰：「有姓無名。」

translations.literal: Song said, "There is surname but no given name."
translations.idiomatic: Song said, "There is surname but no given name."

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，命有司窮冶，索嵩家，得讖書。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of this and ordered the officials to investigate thoroughly; they searched Song's house and obtained the prognostic book.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard and ordered a full investigation; searching Song's house, they found the prognostic book.

sentences.zh: 事連南康公鍬鄰，絜、嵩、鄰皆夷三族，死者百餘人。

translations.literal: The affair implicated Duke Qiao of Nankang, Qiao Lin; Jie, Song, and Lin were all exterminated to the third degree of kinship, and more than a hundred died.
translations.idiomatic: The affair implicated Duke Qiao of Nankang, Qiao Lin; Jie, Song, and Lin were all exterminated to the third degree of kinship—more than a hundred dead.

sentences.zh: 絜在勢要，好作威福，諸將破敵，所得財物皆與分之。

translations.literal: Jie, in a position of power, loved to wield authority and favor; when generals defeated the enemy, the goods taken were all shared with him.
translations.idiomatic: Jie, in power, loved to wield authority; generals who defeated the enemy shared the spoils with him.

sentences.zh: 既死，籍其家，財巨萬。

translations.literal: After his death, his household was inventoried and wealth amounted to tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: After his death, his household was inventoried—wealth in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 帝每言之，則切齒。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor spoke of it, he ground his teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor spoke of him, he ground his teeth.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，樂平戾王丕以憂卒。

translations.literal: On guiyou, Prince Li of Leping, Pi, died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, Prince Li of Leping, Pi, died of grief.

sentences.zh: 初，魏主築白台，高二百餘尺。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Northern Wei ruler built the White Tower, more than two hundred feet high.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Northern Wei ruler had built the White Tower, more than two hundred feet high.

sentences.zh: 丕夢登其上，四顧不見人，命術士董道秀筮之，道秀曰：「大吉。」

translations.literal: Pi dreamed of climbing it, looked all around and saw no one, and ordered the diviner Dong Daoxiu to cast the hexagrams; Daoxiu said, "Great good fortune."
translations.idiomatic: Pi dreamed of climbing it, looked all around and saw no one, and ordered the diviner Dong Daoxiu to cast the hexagrams; Daoxiu said, "Great good fortune."

sentences.zh: 丕默有喜色。

translations.literal: Pi silently showed pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Pi silently looked pleased.

sentences.zh: 及丕卒，道秀亦坐棄市。

translations.literal: When Pi died, Daoxiu was also executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: When Pi died, Daoxiu was also executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 高允聞之，曰：「夫筮者皆當依附爻象，勸以忠孝。

translations.literal: Gao Yun heard of it and said, "Diviners should all rely on the lines and images and counsel loyalty and filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yun heard and said, "Diviners should rely on the lines and images and counsel loyalty and filial piety.

sentences.zh: 王之問道秀也，道秀宜曰：「窮高為亢。

translations.literal: When the prince questioned Daoxiu, Daoxiu should have said, "Extreme height becomes excess.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince questioned Daoxiu, Daoxiu should have said, "Extreme height becomes excess.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「亢龍有悔。」

translations.literal: The Classic of Changes says, "The dragon at the peak has regret."
translations.idiomatic: 《Classic of Changes》 says, "The dragon at the peak has regret."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「高而無民。」

translations.literal: It also says, "High yet without people."
translations.idiomatic: It also says, "High yet without people."

sentences.zh: 皆不祥也，王不可以不戒。』

translations.literal: All are inauspicious; the prince cannot fail to take warning.'
translations.idiomatic: All are inauspicious; the prince cannot fail to take warning.'

sentences.zh: 如此，則王安於上，身全於下矣。

translations.literal: Thus the prince would be secure above and preserve himself below.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the prince would be secure above and preserve himself below.

sentences.zh: 道秀反之，宜其死也。」

translations.literal: Daoxiu did the opposite—it was fitting that he die."
translations.idiomatic: Daoxiu did the opposite—small wonder he died."

sentences.zh: 庚辰，魏主幸廬。

translations.literal: On gengchen, the Northern Wei ruler visited the lodge.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, the Northern Wei ruler visited the lodge.

sentences.zh: 己丑，江夏王義恭進位太尉，領司徒。

translations.literal: On jichou, Prince Gong of Jiangxia, Yigong, was promoted to Grand Commandant and concurrently held the post of Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Prince Gong of Jiangxia, Yigong, was promoted to Grand Commandant and concurrently Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，以侍中、領右衛將軍沈演之為中領軍，左衛將軍范曄為太子詹事。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Attendant-in-Ordinary and Commander of the Right Guard Shen Yanzhi was made Commander of the Central Guard, and Commander of the Left Guard Fan Ye was made Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Attendant-in-Ordinary and Commander of the Right Guard Shen Yanzhi was made Commander of the Central Guard, and Commander of the Left Guard Fan Ye was made Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，立皇子宏為建平王。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Prince Hong was enfeoffed as Prince of Jianping.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, Prince Hong was enfeoffed as Prince of Jianping.

sentences.zh: 三月，甲辰，魏主還宮。

translations.literal: Third month, on jiachen: the Northern Wei ruler returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiachen, the Northern Wei ruler returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，魏主遣司空長孫道生鎮統萬。

translations.literal: On guichou, the Northern Wei ruler sent Minister of Works Changsun Daosheng to garrison Tongwan.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, the Northern Wei ruler sent Minister of Works Changsun Daosheng to garrison Tongwan.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，乙亥，魏侍中、太宰、陽平王杜超為帳下所殺。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on yihai: Northern Wei's Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Mentor, and Prince of Yangping, Du Chao, was killed by those in his tent guard.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on yihai, Northern Wei's Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Mentor, and Prince of Yangping, Du Chao, was killed by his tent guard.

sentences.zh: 六月，魏北部民殺立義將軍衡陽公莫孤，帥五千餘落北走。

translations.literal: Sixth month: the people of Northern Wei's northern region killed General Who Establishes Righteousness Duke Mo of Hengyang, Mo Gu, and led more than five thousand households north in flight.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, people of Northern Wei's northern region killed General Who Establishes Righteousness Duke Mo of Hengyang, Mo Gu, and led more than five thousand households north in flight.

sentences.zh: 遣兵追擊之，至漠南，殺其渠帥，餘徙冀、相、定三州為營戶。

translations.literal: Troops were sent in pursuit to south of the desert; their chieftains were killed and the remainder were relocated to the three provinces of Ji, Xiang, and Ding as garrison households.
translations.idiomatic: Troops pursued them south of the desert, killed their chieftains, and relocated the rest to Ji, Xiang, and Ding as garrison households.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾王慕利延兄子緯世與魏使者謀降魏，慕利延殺之。

translations.literal: Weishi, nephew of King Muli Yan of Tuyuhun, plotted with Northern Wei envoys to surrender to Northern Wei; Muli Yan killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Weishi, nephew of King Muli Yan of Tuyuhun, plotted with Northern Wei envoys to surrender; Muli Yan killed him.

sentences.zh: 是月，緯世弟叱力延等八人奔魏，魏以叱力延為歸義王。

translations.literal: That month, Weishi's younger brother Chil Yan and seven others fled to Northern Wei; Northern Wei made Chil Yan Prince of Guyi.
translations.idiomatic: That month, Weishi's younger brother Chil Yan and seven others fled to Northern Wei, which made Chil Yan Prince of Guyi.

sentences.zh: 沮渠無諱卒，弟安周代立。

translations.literal: Juqu Wuhui died; his younger brother Anzhou succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Wuhui died; his brother Anzhou succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 魏入中國以來，雖頗用古禮祀天地、宗廟、百神，而猶循其舊俗，所祀胡神甚眾。

translations.literal: Since Northern Wei entered China, though they had largely adopted ancient rites to sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temple, and the hundred spirits, they still followed their old customs and the barbarian gods they worshipped were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Since Northern Wei entered China, though they largely adopted ancient rites for Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temple, and the hundred spirits, they still followed old customs and worshipped many barbarian gods.

sentences.zh: 崔浩請存合於祀典者五十七所，其餘復重及小神悉罷之。

translations.literal: Cui Hao requested that fifty-seven shrines conforming to the sacrificial canon be retained, and that the rest, duplicate and minor gods alike, be entirely abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao asked to keep fifty-seven shrines conforming to the sacrificial canon and abolish the rest, duplicate and minor gods alike.

sentences.zh: 魏主從之。

translations.literal: The Northern Wei ruler complied.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei ruler agreed.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸卯，魏東雍州刺史沮渠秉謀反，伏誅。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, on guimao: Northern Wei's governor of Eastern Yongzhou, Juqu Bing, plotted rebellion and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on guimao, Northern Wei's governor of Eastern Yongzhou, Juqu Bing, plotted rebellion and was executed.

sentences.zh: 八月，乙丑，魏主畋於河西，尚書令古弼留守。

translations.literal: Eighth month, on yichou: the Northern Wei ruler hunted west of the river; Minister of the Interior Gu Bi remained on guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on yichou, the Northern Wei ruler hunted west of the river; Minister of the Interior Gu Bi remained on guard.

sentences.zh: 詔以肥馬給獵騎，弼悉以弱者給之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered fat horses given to the hunting cavalry; Bi gave them all weak ones.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered fat horses for the hunting cavalry; Bi gave them all weak ones.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒曰：「筆頭奴敢裁量朕！

translations.literal: The emperor raged, saying, "The brush-headed slave dares to judge me!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged: "The brush-headed slave dares to judge me!

sentences.zh: 朕還台，先斬此奴！」

translations.literal: When I return to court, I shall behead this slave first!"
translations.idiomatic: When I return to court, I shall behead this slave first!"

sentences.zh: 弼頭銳，故帝常以筆目之。

translations.literal: Bi's head was pointed, so the emperor often called him a brush.
translations.idiomatic: Bi's head was pointed, so the emperor often called him a brush.

sentences.zh: 弼官屬惶怖，恐並坐誅。

translations.literal: Bi's staff were terrified, fearing they would be punished together with execution.
translations.idiomatic: Bi's staff were terrified, fearing they would be executed with him.

sentences.zh: 弼曰：「吾為人臣，不使人主盤於游畋，其罪小；

translations.literal: Bi said, "As a subject, if I do not let the ruler indulge in hunting, the crime is small;
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "As a subject, failing to keep the ruler from indulging in the hunt is a small offense;

sentences.zh: 不備不虞，乏軍國之用，其罪大。

translations.literal: if I fail to prepare against the unexpected and leave army and state wanting, the crime is great.
translations.idiomatic: failing to prepare against the unexpected and leaving army and state wanting is a grave offense.

sentences.zh: 今蠕蠕方強，南寇未滅，吾以肥馬供軍，弱馬供獵，為國遠慮，雖死何傷！

translations.literal: Now the Ruru are strong and southern enemies are not yet destroyed; I give fat horses to the army and weak horses to the hunt—for the state's long-term good, what harm if I die!
translations.idiomatic: The Ruru are strong and southern enemies remain; I give fat horses to the army and weak ones to the hunt—for the state's long-term good, what harm if I die!

sentences.zh: 且吾自為之，非諸君之憂也。」

translations.literal: Moreover I did this myself—it is not your concern."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I did this myself—it is not your concern."

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，歎曰：「有臣如此，國之寶也！」

translations.literal: The emperor heard and sighed, "With such a minister, he is the state's treasure!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard and sighed, "With such a minister, the state is blessed!"

sentences.zh: 賜衣一襲，馬二匹，鹿十頭。

translations.literal: He granted one suit of clothes, two horses, and ten deer.
translations.idiomatic: He granted a suit of clothes, two horses, and ten deer.

sentences.zh: 它日，魏主復畋於山北，獲麋鹿數千頭。

translations.literal: Another day the Northern Wei ruler hunted again north of the mountains and took several thousand elk.
translations.idiomatic: Another day the Northern Wei ruler hunted north of the mountains again and took several thousand elk.

sentences.zh: 詔尚書發牛車五百乘以運之。

translations.literal: He ordered the Secretariat to dispatch five hundred ox-carts to transport them.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the Secretariat to dispatch five hundred ox-carts to haul them.

sentences.zh: 詔使已去，魏主謂左右曰：「筆公必不與我，汝輩不如自以馬運之。」

translations.literal: After the edict messenger had gone, the Northern Wei ruler told those beside him, "Brush-head will surely not give them to me—you had better transport them yourselves by horse."
translations.idiomatic: After the messenger left, the Northern Wei ruler told his attendants, "Brush-head will surely refuse—you had better haul them yourselves by horse."

sentences.zh: 遂還。

translations.literal: He then returned.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned.

sentences.zh: 行百餘里，得弼表曰：「今秋谷懸黃，麻菽布野，豬鹿竊食；

translations.literal: After traveling more than a hundred li, he received Bi's memorial saying, "Now autumn grain hangs yellow, hemp and beans cover the fields, and boars and deer steal the crop;
translations.idiomatic: After traveling more than a hundred li, he received Bi's memorial: "Autumn grain hangs ripe, hemp and beans cover the fields, and boars and deer steal the crop;

sentences.zh: 鳥雁侵費，風雨所耗，朝夕三倍。

translations.literal: birds and wild geese consume it, wind and rain waste it—the loss triples morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: birds and wild geese consume it, wind and rain waste it—the loss triples day by day.

sentences.zh: 乞賜矜緩，使得收載。」

translations.literal: I beg compassion and delay so the harvest may be gathered in."
translations.idiomatic: I beg compassion and delay so the harvest may be gathered in."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「果如吾言，筆公可謂社稷之臣矣！」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "It is just as I said—Brush-head may be called a minister of the altars of soil and grain!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Just as I said—Brush-head is truly a pillar of the state!"

sentences.zh: 魏主使員外散騎常侍高濟來聘。

translations.literal: The Northern Wei ruler sent Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier Gao Ji on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei ruler sent Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier Gao Ji on a friendly mission.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，以荊州刺史衡陽王義季為征北大將軍、開府儀同三司、南袞州刺史，以南譙王義宣為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Prince Ji of Hengyang, Yiji, governor of Jingzhou, was made Grand General Who Campaigns North, grand master with honors equal to the Three Excellencies, and governor of Southern Yanzhou; Prince Xuan of Nanqiao, Yixuan, was made governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Prince Ji of Hengyang, Yiji, governor of Jingzhou, was made Grand General Who Campaigns North, grand master with honors equal to the Three Excellencies, and governor of Southern Yanzhou; Prince Xuan of Nanqiao, Yixuan, was made governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，帝以義宣不才，故不用；

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor, considering Yixuan lacking talent, had not used him;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor, deeming Yixuan untalented, had not used him;

sentences.zh: 會稽公主屢以為言，帝不得已用之。

translations.literal: the Princess of Kuaiji repeatedly spoke on his behalf, and the emperor, having no choice, employed him.
translations.idiomatic: the Princess of Kuaiji repeatedly pleaded for him, and the emperor, having no choice, employed him.

sentences.zh: 先賜中詔敕之曰：「師護以在西久，比表求還，今欲聽許，以汝代之。

translations.literal: First he granted a secret edict instructing him, "Shihu has been in the west long; he recently petitioned to return, and I now wish to grant this and replace him with you.
translations.idiomatic: First he sent a secret edict: "Shihu has been in the west long; he recently asked to return, and I now wish to grant it and replace him with you.

sentences.zh: 師護雖無殊績，潔己節用，通懷期物，不恣群下，聲著西土，為士庶所安，論者乃未議遷之。

translations.literal: Shihu, though without special achievements, keeps himself pure and frugal, is broad-minded and expects much of others, does not indulge his subordinates, and his reputation stands in the western lands; gentry and commoners alike are at ease under him, and critics had not yet discussed replacing him.
translations.idiomatic: Shihu, though without special achievements, keeps himself pure and frugal, is broad-minded and demanding of others, does not indulge his subordinates, and is trusted in the west; critics had not yet discussed replacing him.

sentences.zh: 今之回換，更為汝與師護年時一輩，欲各試其能。

translations.literal: This rotation is further because you and Shihu are of the same generation; I wish to test each of you.
translations.idiomatic: This rotation is also because you and Shihu are of the same generation; I wish to test each of you.

sentences.zh: 汝往，脫有一事減之者，既於西夏交有巨礙，遷代之譏，必歸責於吾矣。

translations.literal: If you go and fall short in even one matter, it will greatly harm relations with the western Xia, and the blame for the transfer will surely fall on me.
translations.idiomatic: If you go and fall short in even one matter, it will greatly harm the western frontier, and blame for the transfer will fall on me.

sentences.zh: 此事亦易勉耳，無為使人復生評論也！」

translations.literal: This is easy to strive for—do not give people cause for fresh criticism!"
translations.idiomatic: This is easy to strive for—do not give people fresh cause for criticism!"

sentences.zh: 義宣至鎮，勤自課厲，事亦修理。

translations.literal: When Yixuan reached his post, he diligently applied himself and affairs were well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: When Yixuan reached his post, he applied himself diligently and affairs were well ordered.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，會稽長公主卒。

translations.literal: On gengchen, the Senior Princess of Kuaiji died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, the Senior Princess of Kuaiji died.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾叱力延等請師於魏以討吐谷渾王慕利延，魏主使晉王伏羅督諸軍擊之。

translations.literal: Chil Yan of Tuyuhun and others requested troops from Northern Wei to attack King Muli Yan of Tuyuhun; the Northern Wei ruler sent Prince Fula of Jin to command the armies against him.
translations.idiomatic: Chil Yan of Tuyuhun and others asked Northern Wei for troops against King Muli Yan; the Northern Wei ruler sent Prince Fula of Jin to command the armies against him.

sentences.zh: 九月，甲辰，以沮渠安周為都督涼、河、沙三州諸軍事、涼州刺史、河西王。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on jiachen: Juqu Anzhou was made area commander of military affairs for the three provinces of Liang, He, and Sha, governor of Liangzhou, and Prince of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jiachen, Juqu Anzhou was made area commander of Liang, He, and Sha, governor of Liangzhou, and Prince of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 丁未，魏主如漠南，將襲柔然，柔然敕連可汗遠遁，乃止。

translations.literal: On dingwei, the Northern Wei ruler went south of the desert intending to raid the Rouran; Rouran Khan Chelian fled far away, and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, the Northern Wei ruler went south of the desert to raid the Rouran; Khan Chelian fled far away, and he stopped.

sentences.zh: 敕連尋卒，子吐賀真立，號處羅可汗。

translations.literal: Chelian soon died; his son Tuhu Zhen succeeded and styled himself Khan Chuluo.
translations.idiomatic: Chelian soon died; his son Tuhu Zhen succeeded as Khan Chuluo.

sentences.zh: 魏晉王伏羅至樂都，引兵從間道襲吐谷渾，至大母橋。

translations.literal: Northern Wei's Prince Fula of Jin reached Ledu, led troops by a hidden route to raid Tuyuhun, and reached Damu Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei's Prince Fula of Jin reached Ledu, led troops by a hidden route against Tuyuhun, and reached Damu Bridge.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾王慕利延大驚，逃奔白蘭，慕利延兄子拾寅奔河西；

translations.literal: King Muli Yan of Tuyuhun was greatly alarmed, fled to Bailan, and Muli Yan's nephew Shiyin fled to Hexi;
translations.idiomatic: King Muli Yan of Tuyuhun was greatly alarmed and fled to Bailan; his nephew Shiyin fled to Hexi;

sentences.zh: 魏軍斬首五千餘級，慕利延從弟伏念等帥萬三千落降於魏。

translations.literal: the Wei army took more than five thousand heads; Muli Yan's younger clansman Funian and others led thirteen thousand households in submission to Northern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: the Northern Wei army took more than five thousand heads; Muli Yan's clansman Funian and others led thirteen thousand households in submission.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己卯，以左軍將軍徐瓊為袞州刺史，大將軍參軍申恬為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, on jimao: General of the Left Guard Xu Qiong was made governor of Yanzhou and Grand General aide Shen Tian governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jimao, General of the Left Guard Xu Qiong was made governor of Yanzhou and Grand General aide Shen Tian governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 徙袞州鎮須昌，冀州鎮歷下，恬，謨之弟也。

translations.literal: The Yanzhou garrison was moved to Xuchang and the Jizhou garrison to Lixia; Tian was Mo's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: The Yanzhou garrison moved to Xuchang and the Jizhou garrison to Lixia; Tian was Mo's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丙戌，魏主還平城。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on bingxu: the Northern Wei ruler returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on bingxu, the Northern Wei ruler returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 是歲，沙州牧李竇入朝於魏，魏人留之，以為外都大官。

translations.literal: That year, Governor of Shazhou Li Dou came to court at Northern Wei; the people of Wei detained him and made him Chief Palace Provisioner of the Outer Court.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Governor of Shazhou Li Dou came to court at Northern Wei; they detained him and made him Chief Palace Provisioner of the Outer Court.

sentences.zh: 太子率更令何承天撰《元嘉新歷》，表上之。

translations.literal: Director of the Directorate of Music He Chengtian compiled the Yuanjia New Calendar and submitted it in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Directorate of Music He Chengtian compiled the 《Yuanjia New Calendar》 and submitted it in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 以月食之沖知日所在。

translations.literal: From the opposition at lunar eclipse he knew the sun's position.
translations.idiomatic: From the opposition at lunar eclipse he determined the sun's position.

sentences.zh: 又以中星檢之，知堯時冬至日在須女十度，今在斗十七度。

translations.literal: He also checked by the culminating stars and knew that at the winter solstice in Yao's time the sun was at ten degrees of Maiden; now it is at seventeen degrees of Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Checking by the culminating stars, he found that at the winter solstice in Yao's time the sun stood at ten degrees of Maiden; now it stands at seventeen degrees of Dipper.

sentences.zh: 又測景校二至，差三日有餘，知今之南至日應在斗十三四度。

translations.literal: He also measured shadows to verify the two solstices; the discrepancy was more than three days, showing that today's summer solstice sun should be at thirteen or fourteen degrees of Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Measuring shadows to verify the solstices, he found a discrepancy of more than three days, showing today's summer solstice sun should stand at thirteen or fourteen degrees of Dipper.

sentences.zh: 於是更立新法，冬至徙上三日五時，日之所在，移舊四度。

translations.literal: Thereupon he established a new method: the winter solstice moved up three days and five hours, and the sun's position shifted four degrees from the old reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: He then established a new method: the winter solstice moved up three days and five hours, and the sun's position shifted four degrees from the old reckoning.

sentences.zh: 又月有遲疾，前歷合朔，月食不在朔望；

translations.literal: Also the moon has fast and slow phases; in the previous calendar, new moons did not align and lunar eclipses did not fall on new or full moon;
translations.idiomatic: The moon also has fast and slow phases; in the previous calendar, new moons did not align and lunar eclipses did not fall on new or full moon;

sentences.zh: 今皆以盈縮定其小餘，以正朔望之曰。

translations.literal: now all are fixed by expansion and contraction of the fractional remainder to correct the days of new and full moon.
translations.idiomatic: now all are fixed by expansion and contraction of the fractional remainder to correct the days of new and full moon.

sentences.zh: 詔付外詳之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered it sent outside for detailed review.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered it sent out for detailed review.

sentences.zh: 太史令錢樂之等奏：皆如承天所上，唯月有頻三大，頻二小，比舊法殊為乖異，謂宜仍舊。

translations.literal: Director of Astronomy Qian Yuezhi and others memorialized: all was as Chengtian submitted, except that months frequently had three long periods and frequently two short ones—far different from the old method; they said the old method should remain.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Astronomy Qian Yuezhi and others memorialized: all matched Chengtian's submission except that months frequently had three long periods and two short ones—far different from the old method; they said the old method should remain.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝中之中元嘉二十二年（

translations.literal: Middle period of Great Ancestor Emperor Wen, twenty-second year of Yuanjia (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Liu Song, twenty-second year of Yuanjia (

sentences.zh: 乙酉，公元四四五年）

translations.literal: yiyou, CE 445)
translations.idiomatic: yiyou, CE 445)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛卯朔，始行新歷。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on the xinmao new moon: the new calendar was first put into use.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the xinmao new moon, the new calendar was first put into use.

sentences.zh: 初，漢京房以十二律中呂上生黃鐘，不滿九寸，更演為六十律。

translations.literal: Earlier, Han's Jing Fang, because among the twelve pitch pipes the generation from Zhonglü upward to Huangzhong did not reach nine inches, further derived sixty pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Han's Jing Fang, because generating from Zhonglü upward to Huangzhong among the twelve pitch pipes did not reach nine inches, further derived sixty pitch pipes.

sentences.zh: 錢樂之復演為三百六十律，日當一管。

translations.literal: Qian Yuezhi further derived three hundred sixty pitch pipes, one pipe per day.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Yuezhi further derived three hundred sixty pitch pipes, one per day.

sentences.zh: 何承天立議，以為上下相生，三分損益其一，蓋古人簡易之法，猶如古歷周天三百六十五度四分度之一也。

translations.literal: He Chengtian set forth his view that upper and lower generate each other by adding and subtracting one-third—this was the ancients' simple method, just as the old calendar's circuit of heaven was three hundred sixty-five and one-quarter degrees.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian argued that upper and lower generate each other by adding and subtracting one-third—the ancients' simple method, just as the old calendar's circuit of heaven was three hundred sixty-five and one-quarter degrees.

sentences.zh: 而京房不悟，謬為六十。

translations.literal: But Jing Fang did not understand and wrongly made sixty.
translations.idiomatic: But Jing Fang did not understand and wrongly made sixty.

sentences.zh: 乃更設新率，林鐘長六寸一厘，則從中呂還得黃鐘，十二旋宮，聲韻無失。

translations.literal: He then established a new ratio: Linzhong six inches and one li in length, so that from Zhonglü one returned to Huangzhong; the twelve cyclical modes had no loss of pitch.
translations.idiomatic: He then established a new ratio: Linzhong six inches and one li long, so that from Zhonglü one returned to Huangzhong; the twelve cyclical modes lost no pitch.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以武陵王駿為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: On renchen, Prince Jun of Wuling was made governor of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Prince Jun of Wuling was made governor of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝欲經略關、河，故以駿鎮襄陽。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to plan for the Guan and He regions, and therefore stationed Jun at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to plan for the Guan and He regions and therefore stationed Jun at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 魏主使散騎常侍宋愔來聘。

translations.literal: The Northern Wei ruler sent Attendant Cavalier Song Yin on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei ruler sent Attendant Cavalier Song Yin on a friendly mission.

sentences.zh: 二月，魏主如上黨，西至吐京，討徙叛胡，出配郡縣。

translations.literal: Second month: the Northern Wei ruler went to Shangdang, west to Tujing, punished and relocated rebellious Hu, and assigned them out to commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, the Northern Wei ruler went to Shangdang, west to Tujing, punished and relocated rebellious Hu, and assigned them to commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，立皇禕為東海王，昶為義陽王。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Prince Yi was enfeoffed as Prince of Donghai and Prince Chang as Prince of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Prince Yi was enfeoffed as Prince of Donghai and Prince Chang as Prince of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 三月，庚申，魏主還宮。

translations.literal: Third month, on gengshen: the Northern Wei ruler returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on gengshen, the Northern Wei ruler returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 魏詔：「諸疑獄皆付中書，以經義量決。」

translations.literal: Northern Wei decreed, "All doubtful criminal cases are to be entrusted to the Secretariat and decided by weighing classical principles."
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei decreed, "All doubtful criminal cases are to be entrusted to the Secretariat and decided by classical principles."

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚戌，魏主遣征西大將軍高涼王那等，擊吐谷渾王慕利延於白蘭，秦州刺史代人封敕文、安遠將軍乙烏頭擊慕利延兄子什歸於枹罕。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on gengxu: the Northern Wei ruler sent Grand General Who Pacifies the West Prince Na of Gaoliang and others to attack King Muli Yan of Tuyuhun at Bailan; Governor of Qinzhou Feng Tiwen of the Toba people and General Who Pacifies the Distant Yi Wutou attacked Muli Yan's nephew Shigui at Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on gengxu, the Northern Wei ruler sent Grand General Who Pacifies the West Prince Na of Gaoliang and others against King Muli Yan of Tuyuhun at Bailan; Governor of Qinzhou Feng Tiwen and General Who Pacifies the Distant Yi Wutou attacked Muli Yan's nephew Shigui at Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 河西之亡也，鄯善人以其地與魏鄰，大懼，曰：「通其使人，知我國虛實，取亡必速。」
