translations.literal: When Hexi fell, the people of Shanshan, because their land bordered Northern Wei, were greatly afraid and said, "If we let their envoys pass, they will learn our state's strength and weakness and our destruction will come quickly."
translations.idiomatic: When Hexi fell, the people of Shanshan, bordering Northern Wei, were greatly afraid and said, "If we let their envoys pass, they will learn our strength and weakness and destroy us quickly."

sentences.zh: 乃閉斷道，使者往來，輒抄劫之。

translations.literal: They then closed and blocked the road; whenever envoys came and went, they were robbed.
translations.idiomatic: They closed the road and robbed envoys whenever they passed.

sentences.zh: 由是西域不通者數年。

translations.literal: Hence the Western Regions were cut off for several years.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Western Regions were cut off for several years.

sentences.zh: 魏主使散騎常侍萬度歸發涼州以西兵擊鄯善。

translations.literal: The Northern Wei ruler sent Attendant Cavalier Wan Du Gui to mobilize troops west of Liangzhou to attack Shanshan.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei ruler sent Attendant Cavalier Wan Du Gui to mobilize troops west of Liangzhou against Shanshan.

sentences.zh: 六月，壬辰，魏主北巡。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on renchen: the Northern Wei ruler toured the north.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on renchen, the Northern Wei ruler toured the north.

sentences.zh: 帝謀伐魏，罷南豫州入豫州。

translations.literal: The emperor planned to campaign against Northern Wei and abolished Southern Yuzhou, merging it into Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor planned to campaign against Northern Wei and abolished Southern Yuzhou, merging it into Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，以南豫州刺史南平王鑠為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Prince Shuo of Nanping, governor of Southern Yuzhou, was made governor of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, Prince Shuo of Nanping, governor of Southern Yuzhou, was made governor of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，己未，以尚書僕射孟顗為左僕射，中護軍何尚之為右僕射。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, on jiwei: Vice Director of the Secretariat Meng Kai was made Left Vice Director and Commander of the Central Guard He Shangzhi Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on jiwei, Vice Director of the Secretariat Meng Kai was made Left Vice Director and Commander of the Central Guard He Shangzhi Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 武陵王駿將之鎮，時緣沔諸蠻猶為寇，水陸梗礙；

translations.literal: When Prince Jun of Wuling was about to go to his post, the tribes along the Han still raided and land and water routes were blocked;
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jun of Wuling was about to take his post, tribes along the Han still raided and land and water routes were blocked;

sentences.zh: 駿分軍遣撫軍中兵參軍沈慶之掩擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Jun divided his army and sent Pacifier of the Army Central Command aide Shen Qingzhi in a surprise attack, routing them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Jun divided his army and sent Pacifier of the Army Central Command aide Shen Qingzhi in a surprise attack and routed them.

sentences.zh: 駿至鎮，蠻斷驛道，欲攻隨郡；

translations.literal: When Jun reached his post, the tribes cut the courier road and wished to attack Sui Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: When Jun reached his post, the tribes cut the courier road and tried to attack Sui Commandery;

sentences.zh: 隨郡太守河東柳元景募得六七百人，邀擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Sui Commandery Liu Yuanjing of Hedong recruited six or seven hundred men, intercepted and attacked, and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator of Sui Commandery Liu Yuanjing of Hedong recruited six or seven hundred men, intercepted them, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 遂平諸蠻，獲七萬餘口。

translations.literal: He then pacified the tribes and took more than seventy thousand captives.
translations.idiomatic: He then pacified the tribes and took more than seventy thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 溳山蠻最強，沈慶之討平之，獲三萬餘口，徙萬餘口於建康。

translations.literal: The Yunshan tribes were strongest; Shen Qingzhi campaigned and pacified them, taking more than thirty thousand captives and relocating more than ten thousand to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: The Yunshan tribes were strongest; Shen Qingzhi campaigned and pacified them, taking more than thirty thousand captives and relocating more than ten thousand to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾什歸聞魏軍將至，棄城夜遁。

translations.literal: Shigui of Tuyuhun, hearing the Wei army was about to arrive, abandoned the city and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Shigui of Tuyuhun, hearing the Northern Wei army was coming, abandoned the city and fled by night.

sentences.zh: 八月，丁亥，封敕文入枹罕，分徙其民千家還上邽，留乙烏頭守枹罕。

translations.literal: Eighth month, on dinghai: Feng Tiwen entered Fuhan, relocated a thousand households of its people back to Shanggui, and left Wutou to guard Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on dinghai, Feng Tiwen entered Fuhan, relocated a thousand households back to Shanggui, and left Wutou to guard Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 萬度歸至敦煌，留輜重，以輕騎五千度流沙，襲鄯善。

translations.literal: Wan Du Gui reached Dunhuang, left the baggage train, and with five thousand light cavalry crossed the shifting sands to raid Shanshan.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Du Gui reached Dunhuang, left the baggage train, and with five thousand light cavalry crossed the shifting sands against Shanshan.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，鄯善王真達面縛出降。

translations.literal: On renchen, King Zhenda of Shanshan came out bound in person and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, King Zhenda of Shanshan came out bound and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 度歸留軍屯守，與真達詣平城，西域復通。

translations.literal: Du Gui left troops to garrison and guard, and with Zhenda went to Pingcheng; the Western Regions were open again.
translations.idiomatic: Du Gui left troops to garrison, went with Zhenda to Pingcheng, and the Western Regions were open again.

sentences.zh: 魏主如陰山之北，發諸州兵三分之一，各於其州戒嚴，以須後命。

translations.literal: The Northern Wei ruler went north of the Yin Mountains, mobilized one-third of the troops of each province, and had each province stand on alert awaiting further orders.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei ruler went north of the Yin Mountains, mobilized one-third of each province's troops, and had each province stand on alert awaiting orders.

sentences.zh: 徙諸種雜民五千餘家於北邊，令就北畜牧，以餌柔然。

translations.literal: More than five thousand households of various mixed peoples were relocated to the northern frontier and ordered to pasture livestock in the north as bait for the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: More than five thousand households of various mixed peoples were relocated to the northern frontier to pasture livestock as bait for the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，魏高涼王那軍至寧頭城，吐谷渾王慕利延擁其部落西度流沙。

translations.literal: On renyin, the army of Northern Wei's Prince Na of Gaoliang reached Ningtou City; King Muli Yan of Tuyuhun led his tribes west across the shifting sands.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, the army of Northern Wei's Prince Na of Gaoliang reached Ningtou City; King Muli Yan of Tuyuhun led his tribes west across the shifting sands.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾慕瑰之子被囊逆戰，那擊破之；

translations.literal: Mugui's son Beinang of Tuyuhun fought back; Na routed him;
translations.idiomatic: Mugui's son Beinang of Tuyuhun fought back; Na routed him;

sentences.zh: 被囊遁走，中山公杜豐帥精騎追之，度三危，至雪山，生擒被囊及吐谷渾什歸、乞伏熾磐之子成龍，皆送平城。

translations.literal: Beinang fled; Duke Du of Zhongshan Du Feng led elite cavalry in pursuit, crossed Sanwei, reached Snow Mountain, and captured Beinang alive together with Shigui of Tuyuhun and Qifu Chipan's son Chenglong—all were sent to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Beinang fled; Duke Du of Zhongshan Du Feng led elite cavalry in pursuit, crossed Sanwei to Snow Mountain, and captured Beinang alive with Shigui of Tuyuhun and Qifu Chipan's son Chenglong—all sent to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 慕利延遂西入于闐，殺其王，據其地，死者數萬人。

translations.literal: Muli Yan then went west into Khotan, killed its king, seized the land, and tens of thousands died.
translations.idiomatic: Muli Yan then went west into Khotan, killed its king, seized the land, and tens of thousands died.

sentences.zh: 九月，癸酉，上餞衡陽王義季於武帳岡。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on guiyou: the emperor saw off Prince Ji of Hengyang, Yiji, at Wuzhang Hill.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on guiyou, the emperor saw off Prince Ji of Hengyang, Yiji, at Wuzhang Hill.

sentences.zh: 上將行，敕諸子且勿食，至會所設饌；

translations.literal: As the emperor was about to depart, he ordered his sons not to eat yet and to wait for the feast at the meeting place;
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor was about to depart, he ordered his sons not to eat yet and to wait for the feast at the meeting place;

sentences.zh: 日旰，不至，有饑色。

translations.literal: the sun set and he did not arrive; they showed hunger.
translations.idiomatic: the sun set and he did not arrive; they showed hunger.

sentences.zh: 上乃謂曰：「汝曹少長豐佚，不見百姓艱難。

translations.literal: The emperor then said, "You have grown up in abundance and have not seen the people's hardship.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then said, "You have grown up in abundance and have not seen the people's hardship.

sentences.zh: 今使汝曹識有饑苦，知以節儉御物耳。」

translations.literal: Now I make you know hunger and hardship so you may know to govern things with frugality."
translations.idiomatic: Now I make you know hunger so you may learn to govern with frugality."

sentences.zh: 裴子野論曰：善乎太祖之訓也！

translations.literal: Pei Ziye's commentary says: How excellent is the Great Ancestor's instruction!
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ziye's commentary says: How excellent is the Great Ancestor's instruction!

sentences.zh: 夫侈興於有餘，儉生於不足。

translations.literal: Extravagance arises from surplus; frugality arises from insufficiency.
translations.idiomatic: Extravagance arises from surplus; frugality arises from insufficiency.

sentences.zh: 欲其隱約，莫若貧賤。

translations.literal: If one wishes them to be restrained and modest, nothing is better than poverty and low station.
translations.idiomatic: If one wishes them restrained and modest, nothing beats poverty and low station.

sentences.zh: 習其險限，利以任使；

translations.literal: Accustom them to hardship and danger, and it benefits employing them;
translations.idiomatic: Accustom them to hardship and danger, and they serve well;

sentences.zh: 達其情偽，易以躬臨。

translations.literal: understand their true and false feelings, and it is easy to attend to matters in person.
translations.idiomatic: understand their true feelings, and personal oversight comes easily.

sentences.zh: 太祖若能率此訓也，難其志操，卑其禮秩，教成德立，然後授以政事，則無怠無荒，可播之於九服矣。

translations.literal: If the Great Ancestor could follow this instruction—testing their resolve and conduct, lowering their ritual rank, teaching until virtue was established, and only then entrusting them with governance—then without slackness or neglect it could be spread through the nine domains.
translations.idiomatic: If the Great Ancestor had followed this instruction—testing resolve, lowering rank, teaching until virtue stood firm, and only then entrusting governance—they would have ruled without slackness or neglect, and the lesson could have spread through the nine domains.

sentences.zh: 高祖思固本枝，崇樹襁褓；

translations.literal: Emperor Gao thought to strengthen the root branches and exalted those still in swaddling clothes;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao sought to strengthen the imperial branches and exalted princes still in swaddling clothes;

sentences.zh: 後世遵守，迭據方岳。

translations.literal: later generations observed this and in succession held territorial commands.
translations.idiomatic: later generations followed suit, and princes in succession held territorial commands.

sentences.zh: 及乎泰始之初，升明之季，絕咽於衾衽者動數十人。

translations.literal: By the beginning of Taishi and the end of Shengming, those whose throats were cut upon their bedding numbered several tens.
translations.idiomatic: By the beginning of Taishi and the end of Shengming, dozens had their throats cut in their beds.

sentences.zh: 國之存亡，既不是系，早肆民上，非善誨也。

translations.literal: Since the state's survival no longer depended on them, to set them above the people so early was not good instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Since the state's survival no longer depended on them, setting them above the people so early was poor instruction.

sentences.zh: 魏民間訛言「滅魏者吳」，盧水胡蓋吳聚眾反於杏城，諸種胡爭應之，有眾十餘萬，遣其黨趙綰來上表自歸。

translations.literal: Among the people of Northern Wei a rumor spread that "Wu will destroy Wei"; the Lu River Hu chieftain Gai Wu gathered followers and rebelled at Xingcheng, various Hu tribes vied to join him, and his force exceeded one hundred thousand; he sent his follower Zhao Wan bearing a memorial to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Among the people of Northern Wei a rumor spread that "Wu will destroy Wei"; Lu River Hu chieftain Gai Wu gathered followers and rebelled at Xingcheng, various Hu tribes rallied to him until his force exceeded one hundred thousand, and he sent his follower Zhao Wan with a memorial of submission.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，戊子，長安鎮副將拓跋紇帥眾討吳，紇敗死。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, on wuzi: Deputy garrison commander of Chang'an Tuoba He led troops against Wu; He was defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on wuzi, Deputy Garrison Commander of Chang'an Tuoba He led troops against Wu and was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 吳眾愈盛，民皆渡渭，奔南山。

translations.literal: Wu's forces grew ever stronger; the people all crossed the Wei River and fled to the southern mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Wu's forces grew stronger; the people crossed the Wei River and fled to the southern mountains.

sentences.zh: 魏主發高平敕勒騎赴長安，命將軍叔孫拔領攝並、秦、雍三州兵屯渭北。

translations.literal: The Northern Wei ruler mobilized Gaoping Chile cavalry for Chang'an and ordered General Shusun Ba to take command of the troops of the three provinces of Bing, Qin, and Yong and encamp north of the Wei River.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei ruler mobilized Gaoping Chile cavalry for Chang'an and ordered General Shusun Ba to command the troops of Bing, Qin, and Yong and encamp north of the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 十一月，魏發冀州民造浮橋於碻磝津。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: Northern Wei mobilized the people of Jizhou to build a pontoon bridge at Que'ao Ford.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Northern Wei mobilized the people of Jizhou to build a pontoon bridge at Que'ao Ford.

sentences.zh: 蓋吳遣別部帥白廣平西掠新平，安定諸胡皆聚眾應之。

translations.literal: Gai Wu sent a detached commander, Bai Guang, west to raid Xinping; the various Hu of Anding all gathered followers and joined him.
translations.idiomatic: Gai Wu sent detached commander Bai Guang west to raid Xinping; the various Hu of Anding all rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 又分兵東掠臨晉巴東，將軍章直擊破之，溺死於河者三萬餘人。

translations.literal: He also divided forces east to raid Linjin and Badong; General Zhang Zhi routed them and more than thirty thousand drowned in the river.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent forces east to raid Linjin and Badong; General Zhang Zhi routed them and more than thirty thousand drowned in the river.

sentences.zh: 吳又遣兵西掠至長安，將軍叔孫拔與戰於渭北，大破之，斬首三萬餘級。

translations.literal: Wu again sent troops west to raid as far as Chang'an; General Shusun Ba fought them north of the Wei River, routed them utterly, and took more than thirty thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Wu again sent troops west as far as Chang'an; General Shusun Ba fought them north of the Wei River, routed them, and took more than thirty thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 河東蜀薛永完聚眾以應吳，襲擊聞喜。

translations.literal: Xue Yongwan of the Shu of Hedong gathered followers to join Wu and raided Wenxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yongwan of the Shu of Hedong gathered followers to join Wu and raided Wenxi.

sentences.zh: 聞喜縣無兵仗，令憂惶無計；

translations.literal: Wenxi County had no arms; the magistrate was anxious and at a loss;
translations.idiomatic: Wenxi County had no arms; the magistrate was anxious and at a loss;

sentences.zh: 縣人裴駿帥厲鄉豪擊之，永宗引去。

translations.literal: Pei Jun of the county led the local worthies in attack; Yongzong withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Jun of the county rallied the local worthies and attacked; Yongzong withdrew.

sentences.zh: 魏主命薛謹之子拔糾合宗、鄉，壁於河際，以斷二寇往來之路。

translations.literal: The Northern Wei ruler ordered Xue Jin's son Ba to rally clans and villages, fortify on the river bank, and cut the two rebels' route of communication.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei ruler ordered Xue Jin's son Ba to rally clans and villages, fortify on the river bank, and cut the two rebels' line of communication.

sentences.zh: 庚午，魏主使殿中尚書拓跋處直等將二萬騎討薛永宗，殿中尚書乙拔將三萬騎討蓋吳，西平公寇提將萬騎討白廣平。

translations.literal: On gengwu, the Northern Wei ruler sent Palace Director Tuoba Chuzhi and others with twenty thousand cavalry against Xue Yongzong, Palace Director Yiba with thirty thousand cavalry against Gai Wu, and Duke Ti of Xiping Kou with ten thousand cavalry against Bai Guang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, the Northern Wei ruler sent Palace Director Tuoba Chuzhi with twenty thousand cavalry against Xue Yongzong, Palace Director Yiba with thirty thousand against Gai Wu, and Duke Ti of Xiping Kou with ten thousand against Bai Guang.

sentences.zh: 吳自號天台王，署置百官。

translations.literal: Wu styled himself King of Tiantai and appointed the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: Wu styled himself King of Tiantai and appointed officials.

sentences.zh: 辛未，魏主還宮。

translations.literal: On xinwei, the Northern Wei ruler returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, the Northern Wei ruler returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 魏選六州驍騎二萬，使永昌王仁、高涼王那分將之，為二道，掠淮、泗以北，徙青、徐之民以實河北。

translations.literal: Northern Wei selected twenty thousand elite cavalry from six provinces and had Prince Ren of Yongchang and Prince Na of Gaoliang command them in two columns to raid north of the Huai and Si and relocate the people of Qing and Xu to fill out Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei selected twenty thousand elite cavalry from six provinces and had Prince Ren of Yongchang and Prince Na of Gaoliang lead them in two columns to raid north of the Huai and Si and relocate the people of Qing and Xu to fill out Hebei.

sentences.zh: 癸未，魏主西巡。

translations.literal: On guiwei, the Northern Wei ruler toured the west.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, the Northern Wei ruler toured the west.

sentences.zh: 初，魯國孔熙先博學文史，兼通數術，有縱橫才志；

translations.literal: Earlier, Kong Xixian of Lu was broadly learned in literature and history and also versed in numerology and the arts, with talent and ambition for bold stratagems;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Kong Xixian of Lu was broadly learned in literature and history and versed in numerology, with talent and ambition for bold stratagems;

sentences.zh: 為員外散騎侍郎，不為時所知，憤憤不得志。

translations.literal: he was Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier but was not recognized by his age and chafed in frustrated ambition.
translations.idiomatic: he was Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier but unrecognized by his age and chafed in frustrated ambition.

sentences.zh: 父默之為廣州刺史，以贓獲罪，大將軍彭城王義康為救解，得免。

translations.literal: His father Mozhi was governor of Guangzhou and was convicted of embezzlement; Grand General Prince Kang of Pengcheng, Yikang, secured his release and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mozhi, governor of Guangzhou, was convicted of embezzlement; Grand General Prince Kang of Pengcheng, Yikang, secured his release.

sentences.zh: 及義康遷豫章，熙先密懷報效。

translations.literal: When Yikang was transferred to Yuzhang, Xixian secretly harbored thoughts of repaying the debt.
translations.idiomatic: When Yikang was transferred to Yuzhang, Xixian secretly resolved to repay the debt.

sentences.zh: 且以為天文、圖讖，帝必以非道晏駕，由骨肉相殘，江州應出天子。

translations.literal: He also believed from astronomy and prognostic charts that the emperor would die an unnatural death, that through mutual slaughter among kin a Son of Heaven would arise from Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also believed from astronomy and prognostic charts that the emperor would die unnaturally, and through mutual slaughter among kin a Son of Heaven would arise from Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以范曄志意不滿，欲引與同謀，而熙先素不為曄所重。

translations.literal: Because Fan Ye was dissatisfied in ambition, he wished to draw him into the plot, but Xixian had never been highly regarded by Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Because Fan Ye was dissatisfied, he wished to draw him into the plot, but Xixian had never been highly regarded by Ye.

sentences.zh: 太子中舍人謝綜，曄之甥也，熙先傾身事之。

translations.literal: Heir Apparent Household Aide Xie Zong was Ye's nephew; Xixian devoted himself to serving him.
translations.idiomatic: Heir Apparent Household Aide Xie Zong was Ye's nephew; Xixian devoted himself to Zong.

sentences.zh: 綜引熙先與曄相識。

translations.literal: Zong introduced Xixian to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Zong introduced Xixian to Ye.

sentences.zh: 熙先家饒於財，數與曄博，故為拙行，以物輸之。

translations.literal: Xixian's household was rich in wealth; he often gambled with Ye and deliberately played poorly, losing goods to him.
translations.idiomatic: Xixian's household was wealthy; he often gambled with Ye and deliberately played poorly, losing goods to him.

sentences.zh: 曄既利其財，又愛其文藝，由是情好款洽。

translations.literal: Ye, profiting from his wealth and also loving his literary talent, grew warm and intimate with him.
translations.idiomatic: Ye, profiting from his wealth and loving his literary talent, grew warm and intimate with him.

sentences.zh: 熙先乃從容說曄曰：「大將軍英斷聰敏，人神攸屬，失職南垂，天下憤怨。

translations.literal: Xixian then calmly said to Ye, "The Grand General is heroic, decisive, and keen-witted; men and spirits alike look to him. Deposed to the southern frontier, the realm is angry and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Xixian then calmly said to Ye, "The Grand General is heroic, decisive, and keen-witted; men and spirits alike look to him. Deposed to the southern frontier, the realm is angry and resentful.

sentences.zh: 小人受先君遺命，以死報大將軍之德。

translations.literal: Your humble servant received my late father's charge to repay the Grand General's kindness with my life.
translations.idiomatic: I received my late father's charge to repay the Grand General's kindness with my life.

sentences.zh: 頃人情騷動，天文舛錯，此所謂時運之至，不可推移者也。

translations.literal: Lately popular sentiment is unsettled and the heavens are out of order—this is what is called the arrival of the times' turning, which cannot be shifted.
translations.idiomatic: Lately popular sentiment is unsettled and the heavens are out of order—this is the turning of the times, which cannot be shifted.

sentences.zh: 若順天人之心，結英豪之士，表裡相應，發於肘腋，然後誅除異我，崇奉明聖，號令天下，誰敢不從！

translations.literal: If we follow the hearts of Heaven and men, unite heroic men, act inside and out in concert, strike from close at hand, then purge those unlike us, exalt the wise and sage, and command the realm—who would dare not follow!
translations.idiomatic: If we follow Heaven and men's hearts, unite heroes, act inside and out in concert, strike from close at hand, purge our enemies, exalt the wise, and command the realm—who would dare not follow!

sentences.zh: 小人請以七尺之軀，三寸之舌，立功立事而歸諸君子，太人以為何如？」

translations.literal: Your humble servant asks to use this seven-foot frame and three-inch tongue to establish merit and achievement and leave the credit to you gentlemen—what does the elder think?"
translations.idiomatic: I ask to use this body and tongue to establish merit and leave the credit to you gentlemen—what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 曄甚愕然。

translations.literal: Ye was greatly startled.
translations.idiomatic: Ye was greatly startled.

sentences.zh: 熙先曰：「昔毛玠竭節於魏武，張溫畢議於孫權，彼二人者，皆國之俊乂，豈言行玷缺，然後至於禍辱哉！

translations.literal: Xixian said, "Long ago Mao Jie gave his utmost to Wei Wu and Zhang Wen spoke his mind fully to Sun Quan—both were outstanding men of the state; did they reach ruin and disgrace only after flaws in word and deed!
translations.idiomatic: Xixian said, "Long ago Mao Jie gave his utmost to Cao Cao and Zhang Wen spoke his mind to Sun Quan—both were outstanding men of state; did they reach ruin only after flaws in word and deed!

sentences.zh: 皆以廉直勁正，不得久容。

translations.literal: Both were honest, upright, and firm and could not long be tolerated.
translations.idiomatic: Both were honest, upright, and firm and could not long be tolerated.

sentences.zh: 丈人之於本朝，不深於二主，人間雅譽，過於兩臣，讒夫側目，為日久矣，比肩競逐，庸可遂乎！

translations.literal: The elder's standing in this court is no less than those two lords'; your refined reputation among men surpasses both ministers; slanderers have eyed you askance for long; shoulder to shoulder in rivalry—how could it end well!
translations.idiomatic: Your standing in this court is no less than those two lords'; your reputation surpasses both ministers; slanderers have eyed you askance for long—shoulder to shoulder in rivalry, how could it end well!

sentences.zh: 近者殷鐵一言而劉班碎首，彼豈父兄之仇，百世之怨乎？

translations.literal: Lately Yin Tie spoke one word and Liu Ban's head was shattered—was that feud between fathers and elder brothers, hatred of a hundred generations?
translations.idiomatic: Lately Yin Tie spoke one word and Liu Ban's head was shattered—was that feud between fathers and brothers, hatred of a hundred generations?

sentences.zh: 所爭不過榮名勢利先後之間耳。

translations.literal: What was contested was nothing but the order of glory, fame, and profit.
translations.idiomatic: What was contested was nothing but the order of glory, fame, and profit.

sentences.zh: 及其末也，唯恐陷之不深，發之不早；

translations.literal: At the end they only feared not trapping you deep enough or striking not soon enough;
translations.idiomatic: In the end they only feared not trapping you deep enough or striking not soon enough;

sentences.zh: 戮及百口，猶曰未厭。

translations.literal: slaughter reaching a hundred mouths, they still said it was not enough.
translations.idiomatic: slaughter reaching a hundred mouths, they still said it was not enough.

sentences.zh: 是可為寒心悼懼，豈書籍遠事也哉！

translations.literal: This is enough to chill the heart with dread—is it some distant tale from books!
translations.idiomatic: This is enough to chill the heart with dread—is it some distant tale from books!

sentences.zh: 今建大勳，奉賢哲，圖難地易，以安易危，享厚利，收鴻名，一旦包舉而有之，豈可棄置而不取哉！」

translations.literal: Now to establish great merit, serve the wise and sage, plan difficulty from ease, exchange safety for danger, enjoy rich profit and gather great fame—all in one grasp—how can you cast it aside and not take it!"
translations.idiomatic: Now to establish great merit, serve the wise, plan difficulty from ease, exchange safety for danger, enjoy rich profit and gather great fame—all in one grasp—how can you cast it aside!"

sentences.zh: 曄猶疑未決。

translations.literal: Ye still hesitated undecided.
translations.idiomatic: Ye still hesitated.

sentences.zh: 熙先曰：「又有過於此者，愚則未敢道耳。」

translations.literal: Xixian said, "There is something beyond even this that I dare not speak as a fool."
translations.idiomatic: Xixian said, "There is something beyond even this that I dare not speak."

sentences.zh: 曄曰：「何謂也？」

translations.literal: Ye said, "What is it?"
translations.idiomatic: Ye said, "What is it?"

sentences.zh: 熙先曰：「丈人弈葉清通，而不得連姻帝室，人以犬豕及相遇，而丈人曾不恥之，欲為之死，不亦惑乎！」

translations.literal: Xixian said, "The elder's lineage is pure and distinguished through generations, yet you could not marry into the imperial house; men treat you like dogs and swine, and you never felt shame—yet you wish to die for them—is that not deluded!"
translations.idiomatic: Xixian said, "Your lineage is pure and distinguished through generations, yet you could not marry into the imperial house; men treat you like dogs and swine, and you never felt shame—yet you wish to die for them—is that not deluded!"

sentences.zh: 曄門無內行，故熙先以此激之。

translations.literal: Ye's household lacked proper conduct within, and so Xixian provoked him with this.
translations.idiomatic: Ye's household lacked proper conduct within, and so Xixian provoked him with this.

sentences.zh: 曄默然不應，反意乃決。

translations.literal: Ye was silent and did not reply; his mind turned and the decision was made.
translations.idiomatic: Ye was silent; his mind turned and the decision was made.

sentences.zh: 曄與沈演之並為帝所知，曄先至，必待演之俱入，演之先至，嘗獨被引，曄以此為怨。

translations.literal: Ye and Shen Yanzhi were both known to the emperor; if Ye arrived first he always waited for Yanzhi to enter together; if Yanzhi arrived first he was sometimes summoned alone—Ye resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Ye and Shen Yanzhi were both known to the emperor; if Ye arrived first he always waited for Yanzhi to enter together; if Yanzhi arrived first he was sometimes summoned alone—Ye resented this.

sentences.zh: 曄累經義康府佐，中間獲罪於義康。

translations.literal: Ye had repeatedly served as aide in Yikang's household and in between had offended Yikang.
translations.idiomatic: Ye had repeatedly served in Yikang's household and had once offended him.

sentences.zh: 謝綜及父述，皆為義康所厚，綜弟約聚義康女。

translations.literal: Xie Zong and his father Shu were both favored by Yikang; Zong's younger brother Yue married Yikang's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Zong and his father Shu were both favored by Yikang; Zong's brother Yue married Yikang's daughter.

sentences.zh: 綜為義康記室參軍，自豫章還，申義康意於曄，求解晚隙，復敦往好。

translations.literal: Zong was Yikang's secretariat aide; returning from Yuzhang he conveyed Yikang's intent to Ye, seeking to resolve past grievances and restore warm relations.
translations.idiomatic: Zong was Yikang's secretariat aide; returning from Yuzhang he conveyed Yikang's intent to Ye, seeking to resolve past grievances and restore warm relations.

sentences.zh: 大將軍府史仲承祖，有寵於義康，聞熙先有謀，密相結納。

translations.literal: Grand General's household clerk Zhong Chengzu, favored by Yikang, heard of Xixian's plot and secretly joined with him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General's household clerk Zhong Chengzu, favored by Yikang, heard of Xixian's plot and secretly joined him.

sentences.zh: 丹陽尹徐湛之，素為義康所愛，承祖因此結事湛之，告以密計。

translations.literal: Metropolitan Magistrate of Danyang Xu Zhanzhi had long been loved by Yikang; Chengzu therefore attached himself to Zhanzhi and told him the secret plan.
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan Magistrate of Danyang Xu Zhanzhi had long been loved by Yikang; Chengzu therefore attached himself to Zhanzhi and told him the secret plan.

sentences.zh: 道人法略、尼法靜，皆感義康舊恩，並與熙先往來。

translations.literal: The Daoist Falüe and nun Fajing, both moved by Yikang's old kindness, also associated with Xixian.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist Falüe and nun Fajing, both moved by Yikang's old kindness, also associated with Xixian.

sentences.zh: 法靜妹夫許曜，領隊在台，許為內應。

translations.literal: Fajing's brother-in-law Xu Yao commanded a guard unit at court and was pledged as inside contact.
translations.idiomatic: Fajing's brother-in-law Xu Yao commanded a guard unit at court and was pledged as inside contact.

sentences.zh: 法靜之豫章，熙先付以箋書，陳說圖讖。

translations.literal: When Fajing went to Yuzhang, Xixian entrusted her with letters explaining the prognostic charts.
translations.idiomatic: When Fajing went to Yuzhang, Xixian entrusted her with letters explaining the prognostic charts.

sentences.zh: 於是密相署置，及素所不善者，並入死目。

translations.literal: Thereupon they secretly appointed one another, and those they had long disliked were all entered on the death list.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they secretly appointed one another, and those they had long disliked were all entered on the death list.

sentences.zh: 熙先又使弟休先作檄文，稱：「賊臣趙伯符肆兵犯蹕，禍流儲宰。

translations.literal: Xixian also had his younger brother Xiuxian compose a proclamation stating, "The traitor minister Zhao Bofu rashly raised arms against the imperial procession, and disaster reached the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Xixian also had his brother Xiuxian compose a proclamation: "The traitor minister Zhao Bofu rashly raised arms against the imperial procession, and disaster reached the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 湛之、曄等投命奮戈，即日斬伯符首及其黨與。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi, Ye, and others pledged their lives and seized weapons; that very day they beheaded Bofu and his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi, Ye, and others pledged their lives and seized weapons; that very day they beheaded Bofu and his followers.

sentences.zh: 今遣護軍將軍臧質奉璽綬迎彭城王正位辰極。」

translations.literal: Now we send General Who Protects the Army Zang Zhi bearing the seal and cord to welcome the Prince of Pengcheng to the throne at the pole star."
translations.idiomatic: Now we send General Who Protects the Army Zang Zhi bearing the seal and cord to welcome the Prince of Pengcheng to the throne."

sentences.zh: 熙先以為舉大事宜須以義康之旨諭眾，曄又詐作義康與湛之書，令誅君側之惡，宣示同黨。

translations.literal: Xixian thought that in raising a great affair one must instruct the masses with Yikang's intent; Ye also forged a letter from Yikang to Zhanzhi ordering the execution of evil at the ruler's side, and showed it to the co-conspirators.
translations.idiomatic: Xixian thought a great undertaking required Yikang's authority to instruct the masses; Ye also forged a letter from Yikang to Zhanzhi ordering the execution of evil at the ruler's side, and showed it to the co-conspirators.

sentences.zh: 帝之燕武帳岡也，曄等謀以其日作亂。

translations.literal: When the emperor feasted at Wuzhang Hill, Ye and the others plotted to rebel on that day.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor feasted at Wuzhang Hill, Ye and the others plotted to rebel that day.

sentences.zh: 許曜侍帝，扣刀目曄，曄不敢仰視。

translations.literal: Xu Yao attended the emperor, hand on his sword, eyes on Ye; Ye dared not look up.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yao attended the emperor, hand on his sword, eyes on Ye; Ye dared not look up.

sentences.zh: 俄而座散，徐湛之恐事不濟，密以其謀白帝。

translations.literal: Soon the gathering dispersed; Xu Zhanzhi, fearing the affair would fail, secretly reported the plot to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the gathering dispersed; Xu Zhanzhi, fearing failure, secretly reported the plot to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝使湛之具探取本末，得其檄書，選署姓名，上之。

translations.literal: The emperor had Zhanzhi fully investigate and obtain the whole story, got the proclamation and the list of appointments and names, and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Zhanzhi fully investigate, obtained the proclamation and the list of appointments and names, and submitted them.

sentences.zh: 帝乃命有司收掩窮治。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered the officials to seize, investigate, and prosecute to the full.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered officials to seize, investigate, and prosecute to the full.

sentences.zh: 其夜，呼曄置客省，先於外收綜及熙先兄弟，皆款服。

translations.literal: That night he summoned Ye to the guest quarters; outside, Zong and Xixian's brothers were first seized, and all confessed.
translations.idiomatic: That night he summoned Ye to the guest quarters; outside, Zong and Xixian's brothers were first seized, and all confessed.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使詰問曄，曄猶隱拒；

translations.literal: The emperor sent someone to interrogate Ye; Ye still concealed and denied;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent someone to interrogate Ye; Ye still denied everything;

sentences.zh: 熙先聞之，笑曰：「凡處分、符檄、書疏，皆范所造，雲何於今方作如此抵蹋邪？」

translations.literal: Xixian heard and laughed, saying, "All orders, proclamations, and letters were Fan's work—why only now such evasion and denial?"
translations.idiomatic: Xixian heard and laughed: "All orders, proclamations, and letters were Fan's work—why such evasion only now?"

sentences.zh: 帝以曄墨跡示之，乃具陳本末。

translations.literal: The emperor showed Ye his own handwriting, and he then fully recounted the whole affair.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showed Ye his own handwriting, and he then confessed everything.

sentences.zh: 明日，仗士送付廷尉。

translations.literal: The next day armed guards sent them to the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: The next day armed guards sent them to the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 熙先望風吐款，辭氣不橈。

translations.literal: Xixian, seeing which way the wind blew, confessed fully; his words and bearing did not bend.
translations.idiomatic: Xixian, seeing which way the wind blew, confessed fully; his words and bearing did not bend.

sentences.zh: 上奇其才，遣人慰勉之曰：「以卿之才而滯於集書省，理應有異志，此乃我負卿也。」

translations.literal: The emperor marveled at his talent and sent someone to comfort and encourage him, saying, "With your talent stuck in the Secretariat Archive, it was only natural you should have different ambitions—this is my failing toward you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marveled at his talent and sent someone to comfort him: "With your talent stuck in the Secretariat Archive, different ambitions were only natural—this is my failing toward you."

sentences.zh: 又責前吏部尚書何尚之曰：「使孔熙先年將三十作散騎郎，那不作賊！」

translations.literal: He also rebuked former Minister of Personnel He Shangzhi, saying, "If Kong Xixian at nearly thirty had been made Attendant Cavalier, he would never have become a rebel!"
translations.idiomatic: He also rebuked former Minister of Personnel He Shangzhi: "If Kong Xixian at nearly thirty had been made Attendant Cavalier, he would never have rebelled!"

sentences.zh: 熙先於獄中上書謝恩，且陳圖讖，深戒上以骨肉之禍，曰：「願且勿遺棄，存之中書。

translations.literal: From prison Xixian submitted a memorial thanking for kindness and also set forth the prognostic charts, deeply warning the emperor about the calamity of kin slaughter, saying, "I beg that it not be discarded but kept in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: From prison Xixian submitted a memorial thanking for kindness and set forth the prognostic charts, deeply warning the emperor about kin slaughter: "I beg that it not be discarded but kept in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 若囚死之後，或可追錄，庶九泉之下，少塞釁責。」

translations.literal: If after I die in custody it can someday be recorded, perhaps below in the nine springs my guilt may be somewhat assuaged."
translations.idiomatic: If after I die in custody it can someday be recorded, perhaps in the grave my guilt may be somewhat assuaged."

sentences.zh: 曄在獄，為詩曰：「雖無嵇生琴，庶同夏侯色。」

translations.literal: Ye in prison composed a poem: "Though I lack Ji Kang's zither, I hope to match Xiahou's composure."
translations.idiomatic: Ye in prison composed a poem: "Though I lack Ji Kang's zither, I hope to match Xiahou's composure."

sentences.zh: 曄本意謂入獄即死，而上窮治其獄，遂經二旬，曄更有生望。

translations.literal: Ye had originally meant that entering prison meant immediate death, but the emperor prosecuted the case to the full and twenty days passed; Ye again had hope of life.
translations.idiomatic: Ye had expected prison meant immediate death, but the emperor prosecuted the case fully and twenty days passed; Ye again hoped to live.

sentences.zh: 獄吏戲之曰：「外傳詹事或當長系。」

translations.literal: The prison clerk joked with him, "Outside they say the Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household may be held long-term."
translations.idiomatic: The prison clerk joked: "Outside they say the Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household may be held long-term."

sentences.zh: 曄聞之，驚喜。

translations.literal: Ye heard this and was startled and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Ye heard this and was startled and pleased.

sentences.zh: 綜、熙先笑之曰：「詹事疇昔攘袂瞋目，躍馬顧盼，自以為一世之雄；

translations.literal: Zong and Xixian laughed at him, saying, "The Supervisor of the Household once rolled up his sleeves, glared, leaped on his horse and looked about, thinking himself a hero of the age;
translations.idiomatic: Zong and Xixian laughed: "The Supervisor once rolled up his sleeves, glared, leaped on his horse and looked about, thinking himself a hero of the age;

sentences.zh: 今擾攘紛紜，畏死乃爾！

translations.literal: now in such turmoil and confusion, he fears death to this degree!
translations.idiomatic: now in such turmoil, he fears death like this!

sentences.zh: 設令賜以性命，人臣圖主，何顏可以生存！」

translations.literal: Even if life were granted, having plotted against one's lord as a subject—what face could allow survival!"
translations.idiomatic: Even if life were granted, having plotted against one's lord—what face could allow survival!"

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙未，曄、綜、熙先及其子弟、黨與皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on yiwei: Ye, Zong, Xixian, and their sons, younger brothers, and co-conspirators were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on yiwei, Ye, Zong, Xixian, and their sons, brothers, and co-conspirators were all executed.

sentences.zh: 曄母至市，涕泣責曄，以手擊曄頸，曄色不怍；

translations.literal: Ye's mother came to the marketplace, wept and reproached Ye, struck his neck with her hand; Ye's expression did not change;
translations.idiomatic: Ye's mother came to the marketplace, wept and reproached him, struck his neck; Ye's expression did not change;

sentences.zh: 妹及妓妾來別，曄悲涕流漣。

translations.literal: his sister and concubines came to bid farewell; Ye wept bitterly with streaming tears.
translations.idiomatic: his sister and concubines came to bid farewell; Ye wept bitterly.

sentences.zh: 綜曰：「舅殊不及夏侯色。」

translations.literal: Zong said, "Uncle falls far short of Xiahou's composure."
translations.idiomatic: Zong said, "Uncle falls far short of Xiahou's composure."

sentences.zh: 曄收淚而止。

translations.literal: Ye checked his tears and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Ye checked his tears and stopped.

sentences.zh: 謝約不預逆謀，見兄綜與熙先游，常諫之曰：「此人輕事好奇，不近於道，果銳無檢，未可與狎。」

translations.literal: Xie Yue did not participate in the treasonous plot; seeing his elder brother Zong associating with Xixian, he often remonstrated, saying, "This man treats affairs lightly and loves novelty, is not close to the Way, is indeed sharp and unrestrained—not someone to be intimate with."
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yue did not participate in the plot; seeing his brother Zong associating with Xixian, he often remonstrated: "This man treats affairs lightly and loves novelty, is not close to the Way, is sharp and unrestrained—not someone to be intimate with."

sentences.zh: 綜不從而敗。

translations.literal: Zong did not comply and was ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Zong did not listen and was ruined.

sentences.zh: 綜母以子弟自蹈逆亂，獨不出視。

translations.literal: Zong's mother, because her sons had brought themselves into treason and rebellion, alone did not come out to see them.
translations.idiomatic: Zong's mother, because her sons had brought themselves into treason, alone did not come out to see them.

sentences.zh: 曄語綜曰：「姊今不來，勝人多矣。」

translations.literal: Ye said to Zong, "Your elder sister not coming now puts her above most people."
translations.idiomatic: Ye said to Zong, "Your sister not coming now puts her above most people."

sentences.zh: 收籍曄家，樂器服玩並皆珍麗，妓妾不勝珠翠。

translations.literal: Ye's household was inventoried; musical instruments, garments, and playthings were all rare and splendid; concubines were laden with pearls and jade.
translations.idiomatic: Ye's household was inventoried; musical instruments, garments, and playthings were all rare and splendid; concubines were laden with pearls and jade.

sentences.zh: 母居止單陋，唯有一廚盛樵薪；

translations.literal: His mother lived in plain and mean quarters, with only one kitchen storing firewood;
translations.idiomatic: His mother lived plainly, with only one kitchen storing firewood;

sentences.zh: 弟子冬無被，叔父單布籍。

translations.literal: his younger brother had no quilt in winter; his uncle had only a single cloth mat.
translations.idiomatic: his younger brother had no quilt in winter; his uncle had only a single cloth mat.

sentences.zh: 裴子野論曰：夫有逸群之才，必思沖天之據；

translations.literal: Pei Ziye's commentary says: One who has talent surpassing the crowd must think of a foothold reaching the sky;
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ziye's commentary says: One who surpasses the crowd must think of a foothold reaching the sky;

sentences.zh: 蓋俗之量，則憤常均之下。

translations.literal: measured by common standards, he chafes beneath the ordinary level.
translations.idiomatic: measured by common standards, he chafes beneath the ordinary level.

sentences.zh: 其能守之以道，將之以禮，殆為鮮乎！

translations.literal: Those who can keep to the Way and restrain themselves with ritual—are they not rare!
translations.idiomatic: Those who can keep to the Way and restrain themselves with ritual—are they not rare!

sentences.zh: 劉弘仁、范蔚宗皆忸志而貪權，矜才以徇逆，累葉風素，一朝而隕。

translations.literal: Liu Hongren and Fan Weizong both twisted their ambition and craved power, flaunted talent to pursue rebellion, and families of generations of integrity fell in a single morning.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hongren and Fan Weizong both twisted their ambition and craved power, flaunted talent to pursue rebellion, and families of generations of integrity fell in a single morning.

sentences.zh: 向之所謂智能，翻為亡身之具矣。

translations.literal: What was called intelligence became instead the means of their own destruction.
translations.idiomatic: What was called intelligence became instead the means of their own destruction.

sentences.zh: 徐湛之所陳多不盡，為曄等辭所連引，上赦不問。

translations.literal: Much of what Xu Zhanzhi stated was incomplete; he was implicated by Ye and the others in their confessions, but the emperor pardoned him without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Much of what Xu Zhanzhi stated was incomplete; he was implicated by Ye and the others in their confessions, but the emperor pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 臧質，熹之子也，先為徐、袞二州刺史，與曄厚善；

translations.literal: Zang Zhi was Xi's son; he had formerly been governor of the two provinces of Xu and Yan and was close friends with Ye;
translations.idiomatic: Zang Zhi was Xi's son; he had formerly been governor of Xu and Yan and was close friends with Ye;

sentences.zh: 曄敗，以為義興太守。

translations.literal: when Ye fell he was made grand administrator of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: when Ye fell he was made grand administrator of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 有司奏削彭城王義康爵，收付廷尉治罪。

translations.literal: The officials memorialized to strip Prince Kang of Pengcheng, Yikang, of his title, seize him, and deliver him to the Minister of Justice for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Officials memorialized to strip Prince Kang of Pengcheng, Yikang, of his title and deliver him to the Minister of Justice for punishment.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，詔免義康及其男女皆為庶人，絕屬籍，徙付安成郡；

translations.literal: On dingyou, an edict stripped Yikang and his sons and daughters of rank, making them commoners, cut them from the imperial genealogy, and relocated them to Ancheng Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, an edict stripped Yikang and his sons and daughters of rank, cut them from the imperial genealogy, and relocated them to Ancheng Commandery;

sentences.zh: 以寧朔將軍沈邵為安成相，領兵防守。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the North Shen Shao was made administrator of Ancheng and led troops to guard them.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Pacifies the North Shen Shao was made administrator of Ancheng and led troops to guard them.

sentences.zh: 邵，璞之兄也。

translations.literal: Shao was Pu's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was Pu's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 義康在安成，讀書，見淮南厲王長事，廢書歎曰：「自古有此，我乃不知，得罪為宜也。」

translations.literal: Yikang in Ancheng was reading and came upon the affair of King Li of Huainan; he set the book aside and sighed, "Since antiquity there has been this—I did not know it; my punishment is fitting."
translations.idiomatic: Yikang in Ancheng was reading and came upon the affair of King Li of Huainan; he set the book aside and sighed, "Since antiquity there has been this—I did not know it; my punishment is fitting."

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以前豫州刺史趙伯符為護軍將軍。

translations.literal: On gengxu, former governor of Yuzhou Zhao Bofu was made General Who Protects the Army.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, former governor of Yuzhou Zhao Bofu was made General Who Protects the Army.

sentences.zh: 伯符，孝穆皇后之弟子也。

translations.literal: Bofu was a nephew of Empress Xiaomu.
translations.idiomatic: Bofu was a nephew of Empress Xiaomu.

sentences.zh: 初，江左二郊無樂，宗廟雖有登歌，亦無二舞。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the lands east of the Yangtze the two suburban sacrifices had no music; though the ancestral temple had ascent hymns, it also lacked the two dances.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, east of the Yangtze the two suburban sacrifices had no music; though the ancestral temple had ascent hymns, it also lacked the two dances.

sentences.zh: 是歲，南郊始設登歌。

translations.literal: That year, ascent hymns were first established at the southern suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: That year, ascent hymns were first established at the southern suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 魏安南、平南府移書袞州，以南國僑置諸州多濫北境名號；

translations.literal: Northern Wei's Pacifier of the South and Pacifier of the South offices sent a letter to Yanzhou, stating that the southern state's refugee-established provinces largely misused northern frontier place names;
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei's Pacifier of the South and Pacifier of the South offices wrote Yanzhou that the southern state's refugee-established provinces largely misused northern frontier place names;

sentences.zh: 又欲遊獵具區。

translations.literal: they also wished to hunt at Lake Tai.
translations.idiomatic: they also wished to hunt at Lake Tai.

sentences.zh: 袞州答移曰：「必若因土立州，則彼立徐、揚，豈有其地？

translations.literal: Yanzhou replied, "If one must establish provinces according to the land, then they establish Xu and Yang—do they possess that territory?
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou replied, "If one must establish provinces according to the land, then they establish Xu and Yang—do they possess that territory?

sentences.zh: 復知欲遊獵具區，觀化南國。

translations.literal: We also know you wish to hunt at Lake Tai and observe the transformation of the southern state.
translations.idiomatic: We also know you wish to hunt at Lake Tai and observe the southern state.

sentences.zh: 開館飾邸，則有司存；

translations.literal: Opening lodges and furnishing residences—there are officials for that;
translations.idiomatic: Opening lodges and furnishing residences—there are officials for that;

sentences.zh: 呼韓入漢，厥儀未泯，饋餼之秩，每存豐厚。」

translations.literal: when Huhanye entered Han, that ceremony was not extinguished; the rank of tribute gifts was always kept generous."
translations.idiomatic: when Huhanye entered Han, that ceremony was not extinguished; tribute gifts were always generous."

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝中之中元嘉二十三年（

translations.literal: Middle period of Great Ancestor Emperor Wen, twenty-third year of Yuanjia (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Liu Song, twenty-third year of Yuanjia (

sentences.zh: 丙戌，公元四四六年）

translations.literal: bingxu, CE 446)
translations.idiomatic: bingxu, CE 446)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，庚申，尚書左僕射孟顗罷。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on gengshen: Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Meng Kai was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on gengshen, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Meng Kai was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，魏主軍至東雍州，臨薛永宗壘，崔浩曰：「永宗未知陛下自來，眾心縱弛。

translations.literal: On wuchen, the Northern Wei ruler's army reached Eastern Yongzhou and faced Yongzong's fort; Cui Hao said, "Yongzong does not know Your Majesty has come in person; morale is slack.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, the Northern Wei ruler's army reached Eastern Yongzhou and faced Yongzong's fort; Cui Hao said, "Yongzong does not know Your Majesty has come in person; morale is slack.

sentences.zh: 今北風迅疾，宜急擊之。」

translations.literal: Now the north wind is swift; we should strike at once."
translations.idiomatic: Now the north wind is swift; we should strike at once."

sentences.zh: 魏主從之，庚午，圍其壘。

translations.literal: The Northern Wei ruler complied; on gengwu he besieged the fort.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei ruler agreed; on gengwu he besieged the fort.

sentences.zh: 永宗出戰，大敗，與家人皆赴汾水死。

translations.literal: Yongzong came out to fight, was utterly defeated, and with his family all entered the Fen River and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzong came out to fight, was routed, and with his family drowned himself in the Fen River.

sentences.zh: 其族人安都先據弘農，棄城來奔。

translations.literal: His clansman Andu, who had first held Hongnong, abandoned the city and came over in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Andu, who had held Hongnong, abandoned the city and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 辛未，魏主南如汾陰，濟河，至洛水橋。

translations.literal: On xinwei, the Northern Wei ruler went south to Fenyin, crossed the river, and reached Luoshui Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, the Northern Wei ruler went south to Fenyin, crossed the river, and reached Luoshui Bridge.

sentences.zh: 聞蓋吳在長安北，帝以渭北地無谷草，欲渡渭南，循渭而西。

translations.literal: Hearing that Gai Wu was north of Chang'an, the emperor, because north of the Wei River the land had no grain or grass, wished to cross south of the Wei and follow the Wei west.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Gai Wu was north of Chang'an, the emperor, because north of the Wei River the land had no grain or grass, wished to cross south of the Wei and follow the river west.

sentences.zh: 以問崔浩，對曰：「夫擊蛇者先擊其首，首破則尾不能掉。

translations.literal: He asked Cui Hao, who replied, "In striking a snake one first strikes the head; when the head is broken the tail cannot lash.
translations.idiomatic: He asked Cui Hao, who replied, "In striking a snake one first strikes the head; when the head is broken the tail cannot lash.

sentences.zh: 今蓋吳營去此六十里，輕騎趨之，一日可到，到則破之必矣。

translations.literal: Now Gai Wu's camp is sixty li from here; with light cavalry we can reach it in one day, and once there we shall surely break him.
translations.idiomatic: Now Gai Wu's camp is sixty li from here; with light cavalry we can reach it in one day and break him.

sentences.zh: 破吳，南向長安亦不過一日，一日之乏，未至有傷。

translations.literal: Breaking Wu, marching south on Chang'an takes no more than a day; one day's shortage does not yet do harm.
translations.idiomatic: Breaking Wu, marching south on Chang'an takes no more than a day; one day's shortage does no harm.

sentences.zh: 若從南道，則吳徐入北山，猝未可平。」

translations.literal: If we take the southern route, Wu will slowly enter the northern mountains and cannot quickly be pacified."
translations.idiomatic: If we take the southern route, Wu will slowly enter the northern mountains and cannot quickly be pacified."

sentences.zh: 帝不從，自渭南向長安。

translations.literal: The emperor did not comply and from south of the Wei marched on Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused and from south of the Wei marched on Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，至戲水。

translations.literal: On gengchen he reached Xishui.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen he reached Xishui.

sentences.zh: 吳眾聞之，悉散入北地山，軍無所獲。

translations.literal: Wu's forces heard of this and all scattered into the mountains of Beidi; the army gained nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Wu's forces heard and scattered into the mountains of Beidi; the army gained nothing.

sentences.zh: 帝悔之。

translations.literal: The emperor regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor regretted it.

sentences.zh: 二月，丙戌，帝至長安，丙申，如雍城，歷陳倉，還，如雍城。

translations.literal: Second month, on bingxu, the emperor reached Chang'an; on bingshen he went to Yongcheng, passed through Chencang, returned, and went to Yongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on bingxu, the emperor reached Chang'an; on bingshen he went to Yongcheng, passed through Chencang, returned, and went to Yongcheng.

sentences.zh: 所過誅民、夷與蓋吳通謀者。

translations.literal: Wherever he passed he executed commoners and tribesmen who had plotted with Gai Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he passed he executed commoners and tribesmen who had plotted with Gai Wu.

sentences.zh: 乙拔等諸軍大破蓋吳於杏城，吳復遣使上表求援。

translations.literal: The armies of Yiba and others routed Gai Wu utterly at Xingcheng; Wu again sent envoys with a memorial requesting aid.
translations.idiomatic: The armies of Yiba and others routed Gai Wu at Xingcheng; Wu again sent envoys requesting aid.

sentences.zh: 詔以吳為都督關、隴諸軍事、雍州刺史、北地公；

translations.literal: An edict made Wu area commander of military affairs for Guan and Long, governor of Yongzhou, and Duke of Beidi;
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Wu area commander of Guan and Long, governor of Yongzhou, and Duke of Beidi;

sentences.zh: 使雍、梁二州發兵屯境上，為吳聲援；

translations.literal: ordered the two provinces of Yong and Liang to mobilize troops and encamp on the border as support for Wu;
translations.idiomatic: ordered Yong and Liang to mobilize troops on the border as support for Wu;

sentences.zh: 遣使賜吳印一百二十一紐，使吳隨宜假授。

translations.literal: sent envoys granting Wu one hundred twenty-one seals of office for provisional appointment as he saw fit.
translations.idiomatic: sent envoys granting Wu one hundred twenty-one seals for provisional appointment as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 初，林邑王范陽邁，雖遣使入貢，而寇盜不絕，所貢亦薄陋；

translations.literal: Earlier, King Fanyang Mai of Linyi, though sending envoys to pay tribute, never ceased raiding and plundering, and what was offered was also meager;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, King Fanyang Mai of Linyi, though sending tribute envoys, never ceased raiding, and what was offered was meager;

sentences.zh: 帝遣交州刺史檀和之討之。

translations.literal: the emperor sent Governor of Jiaozhou Tan Hezhi to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor sent Governor of Jiaozhou Tan Hezhi against him.

sentences.zh: 南陽宗愨，家世儒素，愨獨好武事，常言「願乘長風破萬里浪」。

translations.literal: Zong Que of Nanyang came from a family of Confucian plainness, but Que alone loved military affairs and often said, "I wish to ride the long wind and break ten thousand li of waves."
translations.idiomatic: Zong Que of Nanyang came from a Confucian family, but Que alone loved military affairs and often said, "I wish to ride the long wind and break ten thousand li of waves."

sentences.zh: 及和之伐林邑，愨自奮請從軍。

translations.literal: When Hezhi campaigned against Linyi, Que volunteered eagerly to join the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Hezhi campaigned against Linyi, Que volunteered to join the army.

sentences.zh: 詔以愨為振武將軍，和之遣愨為前鋒。

translations.literal: An edict made Que General Who Shakes Might, and Hezhi sent Que as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Que General Who Shakes Might, and Hezhi sent him as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 陽邁聞軍出，遣使上表，請還所掠日南民，輸金一萬斤，銀十萬斤。

translations.literal: Yang Mai, hearing the army had marched out, sent envoys with a memorial requesting return of the people of Rinan he had seized and offering ten thousand jin of gold and one hundred thousand jin of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Mai, hearing the army had marched, sent envoys requesting return of the people of Rinan he had seized and offering ten thousand jin of gold and one hundred thousand jin of silver.

sentences.zh: 帝詔和之：「若陽邁果有款誠，亦許其歸順」和之至朱梧戍，遣府戶曹參軍姜仲基等詣陽邁，陽邁執之；

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Hezhi, "If Yang Mai truly shows sincerity, his submission may also be granted." Hezhi reached Zhuwu Fort and sent Household Affairs Aide Jiang Zhongji and others to Yang Mai; Yang Mai seized them;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Hezhi, "If Yang Mai truly shows sincerity, his submission may be granted." Hezhi reached Zhuwu Fort and sent Household Affairs Aide Jiang Zhongji and others to Yang Mai; Yang Mai seized them;

sentences.zh: 和之乃進軍圍林邑將范扶龍於區粟城。

translations.literal: Hezhi then advanced and besieged Linyi general Fan Fulong at Qu Su City.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhi then advanced and besieged Linyi general Fan Fulong at Qu Su City.

sentences.zh: 陽邁遣其將范毘沙達救之，宗愨潛兵迎擊毘沙達，破之。

translations.literal: Yang Mai sent his general Fan Bishada to the rescue; Zong Que with hidden troops intercepted and attacked Bishada and routed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Mai sent General Fan Bishada to the rescue; Zong Que intercepted Bishada with hidden troops and routed him.

sentences.zh: 魏主與崔浩皆信重寇謙之，奉其道。

translations.literal: The Northern Wei ruler and Cui Hao both trusted and honored Kou Qianzhi and followed his Way.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei ruler and Cui Hao both trusted and honored Kou Qianzhi and followed his Way.

sentences.zh: 浩素不喜佛法，每言於魏主，以為佛法虛誕，為世費害，宜悉除之。

translations.literal: Hao had never liked Buddhism and often told the Northern Wei ruler that Buddhism was empty and false, a worldly waste and harm, and should be entirely abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Hao had never liked Buddhism and often told the Northern Wei ruler that Buddhism was empty and false, a worldly waste and harm, and should be abolished.

sentences.zh: 及魏主討蓋吳，至長安，入佛寺，沙門飲從官酒；

translations.literal: When the Northern Wei ruler campaigned against Gai Wu and reached Chang'an, he entered a Buddhist temple where monks had drunk the attendants' wine;
translations.idiomatic: When the Northern Wei ruler campaigned against Gai Wu and reached Chang'an, he entered a Buddhist temple where monks had drunk the attendants' wine;

sentences.zh: 從官入其室，見大有兵器，出以白帝。

translations.literal: attendants entered their rooms and saw many weapons; they went out and reported to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: attendants entered their rooms and found many weapons; they reported to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「此非沙門所用，必與蓋吳通謀，欲為亂耳！」

translations.literal: The emperor raged, "These are not for monks' use—they must have plotted with Gai Wu and intend rebellion!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged, "These are not for monks—they must have plotted with Gai Wu and intend rebellion!"

sentences.zh: 命有司案誅闔寺沙門，閱其財產，大得釀具及州郡牧守、富人所寄藏物以萬計，又為窟室以匿婦子。

translations.literal: He ordered officials to investigate and execute all the monks of the entire temple; examining their property they found brewing equipment in great quantity and goods entrusted for storage by governors and the wealthy numbering in the tens of thousands, and also cave rooms to hide wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered officials to execute all the monks of the temple; examining their property they found brewing equipment and goods entrusted by governors and the wealthy numbering in the tens of thousands, and cave rooms to hide wives and children.

sentences.zh: 浩因說帝悉誅天下沙門，毀諸經像，帝從之。

translations.literal: Hao therefore urged the emperor to execute all monks under Heaven and destroy all sutras and images; the emperor complied.
translations.idiomatic: Hao urged the emperor to execute all monks under Heaven and destroy all sutras and images; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 寇謙之與浩固爭，浩不從。

translations.literal: Kou Qianzhi firmly argued with Hao; Hao did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Qianzhi argued with Hao; Hao would not listen.

sentences.zh: 先盡誅長安沙門，焚毀經像，並敕留台下四方，令一用長安法。

translations.literal: First all Chang'an monks were executed and sutras and images burned; an order also went to the four directions from the capital to apply the Chang'an method uniformly.
translations.idiomatic: First all Chang'an monks were executed and sutras and images burned; an order also went to the four directions from the capital to apply the Chang'an method uniformly.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「昔後漢荒君，信惑邪偽以亂天常，自古九州之中，未嘗有此。

translations.literal: The edict said, "Long ago the reckless ruler of Later Han believed perverse falsehoods and disturbed Heaven's constant order; since antiquity within the nine provinces there has never been this.
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "Long ago the reckless ruler of Later Han believed perverse falsehoods and disturbed Heaven's order; since antiquity within the nine provinces there has never been this.

sentences.zh: 夸誕大言，不本人情，叔季之世，莫不眩焉。

translations.literal: Boastful and extravagant words, not rooted in human feeling—in decadent ages none failed to be dazzled.
translations.idiomatic: Boastful extravagant words, not rooted in human feeling—in decadent ages none failed to be dazzled.

sentences.zh: 由是政教不行，禮義大壞，九服之內，鞠為丘墟。

translations.literal: Hence government and teaching did not prevail, ritual and righteousness were greatly ruined, and within the nine domains all became wasteland.
translations.idiomatic: Hence government and teaching failed, ritual and righteousness collapsed, and within the nine domains all became wasteland.

sentences.zh: 朕承天緒，欲除偽定真，復羲、農之治。

translations.literal: We inherit Heaven's thread and wish to remove the false and establish the true, restoring the governance of Fu Xi and Shen Nong.
translations.idiomatic: We inherit Heaven's mandate and wish to remove the false and establish the true, restoring the governance of Fu Xi and Shen Nong.

sentences.zh: 其一切蕩除，滅其蹤跡。

translations.literal: Let all be swept away and their traces extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Let all be swept away and their traces extinguished.

sentences.zh: 自今已後，敢有事胡神及造形像泥人、銅人者朱。

translations.literal: From now on, whoever dares serve barbarian gods or make images of clay or bronze shall be executed.
translations.idiomatic: From now on, whoever dares serve barbarian gods or make images of clay or bronze shall be executed.

sentences.zh: 有非常之人，然後能行非常之事，非朕孰能去此歷代之偽物？

translations.literal: Only an extraordinary man can perform extraordinary deeds—who but We can remove these false things of successive ages?
translations.idiomatic: Only an extraordinary man can perform extraordinary deeds—who but We can remove these false things of successive ages?

sentences.zh: 有司宣告征鎮諸軍、刺史，諸有浮圖形像及胡經，皆擊破焚燒，沙門無少長悉坑之！」

translations.literal: Officials are to proclaim to campaigning armies and garrisons and to governors: wherever there are Buddhist images and barbarian sutras, all are to be smashed and burned, and monks young and old all buried alive!"
translations.idiomatic: Officials are to proclaim to armies and governors: wherever there are Buddhist images and barbarian sutras, all are to be smashed and burned, and monks young and old all buried alive!"

sentences.zh: 太子晃素好佛法，屢諫不聽，乃緩宣詔書，使遠近豫聞之，得各為計。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Huang had long loved Buddhism and remonstrated repeatedly without being heard; he then delayed proclaiming the edict so that far and near might hear in advance and each make plans.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Huang had long loved Buddhism and remonstrated repeatedly without being heard; he then delayed proclaiming the edict so that far and near might hear in advance and each make plans.

sentences.zh: 沙門多亡匿獲免，或收藏經像，唯塔廟在魏境者無復孑遺。

translations.literal: Many monks fled and hid and were spared, or concealed sutras and images; only pagodas and temples within Northern Wei territory were left with nothing surviving.
translations.idiomatic: Many monks fled and hid and were spared, or concealed sutras and images; only pagodas and temples within Northern Wei territory were left with nothing surviving.

sentences.zh: 魏主徙長安工巧二千家於平城。

translations.literal: The Northern Wei ruler relocated two thousand artisan households from Chang'an to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei ruler relocated two thousand artisan households from Chang'an to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 還，至洛水，分軍誅李閏叛羌。

translations.literal: Returning, he reached the Luo River and divided the army to execute the rebellious Qiang of Li Run.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he reached the Luo River and divided the army to execute the rebellious Qiang of Li Run.

sentences.zh: 太原顏白鹿私入魏境，為魏人所得，將殺之，詐雲青州刺史杜驥使其歸誠。

translations.literal: Yan Bailu of Taiyuan privately entered Northern Wei territory, was captured by the people of Wei, and about to be killed feigned that Governor of Qingzhou Du Ji had sent him to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Bailu of Taiyuan privately entered Northern Wei territory, was captured, and about to be killed feigned that Governor of Qingzhou Du Ji had sent him to submit.

sentences.zh: 魏人送白鹿詣平城，魏主喜曰：「我外家也。」

translations.literal: The people of Wei sent Bailu to Pingcheng; the Northern Wei ruler was pleased and said, "My mother's family."
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei sent Bailu to Pingcheng; the Northern Wei ruler was pleased and said, "My mother's family."

sentences.zh: 使崔浩作書與驥，且命永昌王仁、高涼王那將兵迎驥，攻冀州刺史申恬於歷城；

translations.literal: He had Cui Hao write to Ji and also ordered Prince Ren of Yongchang and Prince Na of Gaoliang to lead troops to welcome Ji and attack Governor of Jizhou Shen Tian at Licheng;
translations.idiomatic: He had Cui Hao write to Ji and ordered Prince Ren of Yongchang and Prince Na of Gaoliang to lead troops to welcome Ji and attack Governor of Jizhou Shen Tian at Licheng;

sentences.zh: 杜驥遣其府司馬夏侯祖歡等將兵救歷城。

translations.literal: Du Ji sent his aide Xiahou Zuhuan and others with troops to rescue Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ji sent his aide Xiahou Zuhuan and others to rescue Licheng.

sentences.zh: 魏人遂寇袞、青、冀三州，至清東而還；

translations.literal: The people of Wei then raided the three provinces of Yan, Qing, and Ji, reaching Qingdong and returning;
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei then raided Yan, Qing, and Ji, reaching Qingdong and returning;

sentences.zh: 殺掠甚眾，北邊騷動。

translations.literal: killing and plundering in great numbers; the northern frontier was in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: killing and plundering in great numbers; the northern frontier was in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 帝以魏寇為憂，咨訪群臣。

translations.literal: The emperor, troubled by Northern Wei raids, consulted the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, troubled by Northern Wei raids, consulted the ministers.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞何承天上表，以為：「凡備匈奴之策，不過二科：武夫盡征伐之謀，儒生講和親之約。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief He Chengtian submitted a memorial holding that: "All policies for guarding against the Xiongnu amount to no more than two categories: warriors exhaust plans of campaign, Confucians discourse on marriage alliances.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief He Chengtian submitted a memorial: "All policies for guarding against the Xiongnu amount to two categories: warriors exhaust plans of campaign, Confucians discourse on marriage alliances.

sentences.zh: 今若欲追蹤衛、霍，自非大田淮、泗，內實青、徐，使民有贏儲，野有積穀，然後發精卒十萬，一舉蕩夷，則不足為也。

translations.literal: If now one wishes to follow Wei Qing and Huo Qubing, unless one first farms greatly on the Huai and Si, fills Qing and Xu within, makes the people have surplus stores and the fields accumulated grain, and then sends one hundred thousand elite troops to sweep the barbarians away in one stroke—it is not enough.
translations.idiomatic: If one wishes to follow Wei Qing and Huo Qubing, unless one first farms greatly on the Huai and Si, fills Qing and Xu within, makes the people surplus in stores and the fields full of grain, and then sends one hundred thousand elite troops to sweep the barbarians away—it is not enough.

sentences.zh: 若但欲遣軍追討，報其侵暴，則彼必輕騎奔走，不肯會戰。

translations.literal: If one only wishes to send armies in pursuit to repay their invasion and violence, they will surely flee on light cavalry and refuse to join battle.
translations.idiomatic: If one only sends armies in pursuit to repay their raids, they will flee on light cavalry and refuse battle.

sentences.zh: 徒興巨費，不損於彼，報復之役，將遂無已。

translations.literal: One only raises vast expense without harming them; campaigns of reprisal will never end.
translations.idiomatic: One only raises vast expense without harming them; campaigns of reprisal will never end.

sentences.zh: 斯策之最末者也。

translations.literal: This is the lowest of strategies.
translations.idiomatic: This is the worst strategy.

sentences.zh: 安邊固守，於計為長。

translations.literal: Securing the frontier and holding firm is the superior plan.
translations.idiomatic: Securing the frontier and holding firm is the superior plan.

sentences.zh: 臣竊以曹、孫之霸，才均智敵，江、淮之間，不居各數百里。

translations.literal: Your servant ventures to think that in the hegemony of Cao and Sun, talents were equal and wits matched, yet between the Yangtze and Huai each held no more than several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant ventures to think that in the hegemony of Cao and Sun, talents were equal and wits matched, yet between the Yangtze and Huai each held no more than several hundred li.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 斥候之郊，非耕牧之地，故堅壁清野以俟其來，整甲繕兵以乘其弊；

translations.literal: The borderlands of scouts and outposts are not fields for farming and grazing; therefore fortify walls and clear the countryside to await their coming, repair armor and sharpen weapons to exploit their weakness;
translations.idiomatic: The borderlands of scouts are not fields for farming; therefore fortify walls and clear the countryside to await them, repair armor and sharpen weapons to exploit their weakness;

sentences.zh: 保民全境，不出此塗。

translations.literal: protecting the people and securing the whole territory—there is no path outside this.
translations.idiomatic: protecting the people and securing the whole territory—there is no path outside this.

sentences.zh: 要而歸之，其策有四：一曰移遠就近。

translations.literal: In sum, there are four policies: first, move the distant near.
translations.idiomatic: In sum, there are four policies: first, move the distant near.

sentences.zh: 今青、兗舊民及冀州新附，在界首者三萬餘家，可悉徙置大峴之南，以實內地。

translations.literal: Now the old inhabitants of Qing and Yan and the newly attached of Jizhou on the border—more than thirty thousand households—may all be relocated south of Great Xian to fill the interior.
translations.idiomatic: Now the old inhabitants of Qing and Yan and the newly attached of Jizhou on the border—more than thirty thousand households—may all be relocated south of Great Xian to fill the interior.

sentences.zh: 二曰多築城邑以居新徙之家，假其經用，春夏佃牧，秋冬入保。

translations.literal: Second, build many walled towns to house the newly relocated families, lend them capital for expenses, farm and pasture in spring and summer, and enter the fortifications in autumn and winter.
translations.idiomatic: Second, build many walled towns for the relocated families, lend them capital, farm and pasture in spring and summer, and enter the fortifications in autumn and winter.

sentences.zh: 寇至之時，一城千家，堪戰之士，不下二千，其餘羸弱，猶能登陴鼓噪，足抗群虜三萬矣。

translations.literal: When raiders come, one town of a thousand households has no fewer than two thousand men fit for battle; the rest, though weak, can still mount the walls and beat drums and shout—enough to resist thirty thousand of the enemy horde.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders come, one town of a thousand households has no fewer than two thousand men fit for battle; the rest, though weak, can still mount the walls and beat drums and shout—enough to resist thirty thousand of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 三曰纂偶車牛以載糧械。

translations.literal: Third, pair oxen and carts to carry grain and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Third, pair oxen and carts to carry grain and weapons.

sentences.zh: 計千家之資，不下五百耦牛，為車五百兩，參合鉤連以衛其眾；

translations.literal: Calculating the resources of a thousand households, there are no fewer than five hundred yoked ox teams, making five hundred carts, linked and chained together to guard the multitude;
translations.idiomatic: A thousand households have no fewer than five hundred yoked ox teams, making five hundred carts linked and chained to guard the multitude;

sentences.zh: 設使城不可固，平行趨險，賊所不能幹，有急征發，信宿可聚。

translations.literal: if the town cannot be held, they move on level ground or hurry to difficult terrain where raiders cannot reach them; in emergency they can be mobilized and gather within two nights.
translations.idiomatic: if the town cannot be held, they move on level ground or hurry to difficult terrain where raiders cannot reach them; in emergency they can gather within two nights.

sentences.zh: 四曰計丁課仗。

translations.literal: Fourth, assess households and levy weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, assess households and levy weapons.

sentences.zh: 凡戰士二千，隨其便能，各自有仗，素所服習，銘刻由己，還保輸之於庫，出行請以自新。

translations.literal: For every two thousand warriors, according to each man's ability he has his own weapon, what he is accustomed to and trained in, marked with his own name; returning to the fort he deposits it in the arsenal, and when going out he requests it anew.
translations.idiomatic: For every two thousand warriors, each has his own weapon suited to his ability, what he is trained in, marked with his name; returning to the fort he deposits it in the arsenal, and when going out he requests it anew.

sentences.zh: 弓簳利鐵，民不得者，官以漸充之。

translations.literal: Bows, arrows, and sharp iron—what the people lack, the state gradually supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Bows, arrows, and sharp iron—what the people lack, the state gradually supplies.

sentences.zh: 數年之內，軍用粗備矣。

translations.literal: Within several years, military supplies will be roughly complete.
translations.idiomatic: Within several years, military supplies will be roughly complete.

sentences.zh: 近郡之師，遠屯清、濟，功費既重，嗟怨亦深，以臣料之，未若即用彼眾之易也。

translations.literal: Armies from nearby commanderies stationed far at Qing and Ji—the labor and expense are already heavy and resentment deep; by your servant's estimate, it is not as easy as directly using those masses there.
translations.idiomatic: Armies from nearby commanderies stationed far at Qing and Ji—the labor and expense are heavy and resentment deep; by my estimate, it is not as easy as directly using those masses there.

sentences.zh: 今因民所利，導而帥之，兵強而敵不戒，國富而民不勞，比於優復隊伍，坐食糧廩者，不可同年而校矣。」

translations.literal: Now following what benefits the people, guiding and leading them—army strong while the enemy is unguarded, state rich while the people are not worn—compared with exempted companies sitting and eating from the granaries, they cannot be weighed in the same year."
translations.idiomatic: Now following what benefits the people and leading them—army strong while the enemy is unguarded, state rich while the people are not worn—compared with exempted companies eating from the granaries, they cannot be weighed in the same scale."

sentences.zh: 魏金城邊固、天水梁會，與秦、益雜民萬餘戶據上邽東城反，攻逼西城。

translations.literal: Northern Wei's Bian Gu of Jincheng and Liang Hui of Tianshui, with more than ten thousand mixed households of Qin and Yi, seized Shanggui's eastern city and rebelled, pressing the western city.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei's Bian Gu of Jincheng and Liang Hui of Tianshui, with more than ten thousand mixed households of Qin and Yi, seized Shanggui's eastern city and rebelled, pressing the western city.

sentences.zh: 秦、益二州刺史封敕文拒卻之。

translations.literal: Governors of Qin and Yi Feng Tiwen repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: Governors of Qin and Yi Feng Tiwen repelled them.

sentences.zh: 氐、羌萬餘人，休官、屠各二萬餘人皆起兵應固、會，敕文擊固，斬之，餘眾推會為主，與敕文相攻。

translations.literal: More than ten thousand Di and Qiang and more than twenty thousand Xiuguan and Tuge all raised troops to join Gu and Hui; Tiwen attacked Gu and beheaded him, and the survivors made Hui leader and fought Tiwen.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand Di and Qiang and more than twenty thousand Xiuguan and Tuge all raised troops to join Gu and Hui; Tiwen attacked Gu and beheaded him, and the survivors made Hui leader and fought Tiwen.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲申，魏主至長安。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on jiashen: the Northern Wei ruler reached Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on jiashen, the Northern Wei ruler reached Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 丁未，大赦。

translations.literal: On dingwei, a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 仇池人李洪聚眾，自言應王。

translations.literal: Li Hong of Qiuchi gathered followers and declared himself destined to rule.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hong of Qiuchi gathered followers and declared himself destined to rule.

sentences.zh: 梁會求救於氐王楊文德，文德曰：「兩雄不並立，若須我者，宜殺洪。」

translations.literal: Hui requested aid from Di King Yang Wendé; Wendé said, "Two heroes cannot stand together; if you need me, you should kill Hong."
translations.idiomatic: Hui requested aid from Di King Yang Wendé; Wendé said, "Two heroes cannot stand together; if you need me, you should kill Hong."

sentences.zh: 會誘洪斬之，送首於文德。
