translations.literal: Hui lured Hong and beheaded him, sending the head to Wendé.
translations.idiomatic: Hui lured Hong and beheaded him, sending the head to Wendé.

sentences.zh: 五月，癸亥，魏主遣安豐公閭根帥騎赴上邽，未至，會棄東城走。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on guihai: the Northern Wei ruler sent Duke Gen of Anfeng Lü with cavalry to Shanggui; before he arrived, Hui abandoned the eastern city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on guihai, the Northern Wei ruler sent Duke Gen of Anfeng Lü with cavalry to Shanggui; before he arrived, Hui abandoned the eastern city and fled.

sentences.zh: 敕文先掘重塹於外，嚴兵守之，格鬥從夜至旦。

translations.literal: Tiwen first dug a deep moat outside and guarded it with strict troops; they fought from night until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Tiwen first dug a deep moat outside and guarded it strictly; they fought from night until dawn.

sentences.zh: 敕文曰：「賊知無生路，致死於我，多殺傷士卒，未易克也。」

translations.literal: Tiwen said, "The rebels know they have no way to live and will fight to the death against us, killing and wounding many soldiers—it is not easy to overcome them."
translations.idiomatic: Tiwen said, "The rebels know they have no way out and will fight to the death, killing and wounding many soldiers—it is not easy to overcome them."

sentences.zh: 乃以白虎幡宣告會眾，降者赦之，會眾遂潰；

translations.literal: He then proclaimed to Hui's followers with the white tiger banner that those who surrendered would be spared; Hui's followers then collapsed;
translations.idiomatic: He then proclaimed to Hui's followers with the white tiger banner that those who surrendered would be spared; Hui's followers collapsed;

sentences.zh: 分兵追討，悉平之。

translations.literal: divided troops to pursue and campaign, and pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: he divided troops to pursue and pacified them all.

sentences.zh: 略陽人王元達聚眾屯松多川，敕文又討平之。

translations.literal: Wang Yuanda of Lueyang gathered followers and encamped at Songduo River; Tiwen again campaigned and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuanda of Lueyang gathered followers at Songduo River; Tiwen again campaigned and pacified him.

sentences.zh: 蓋吳收兵屯杏城，自號秦地王，聲勢復振。

translations.literal: Gai Wu gathered troops and encamped at Xingcheng, styled himself King of Qin Land, and his momentum revived.
translations.idiomatic: Gai Wu gathered troops at Xingcheng, styled himself King of Qin Land, and his momentum revived.

sentences.zh: 魏主遣永昌王仁、高涼王那督北道諸軍討之。

translations.literal: The Northern Wei ruler sent Prince Ren of Yongchang and Prince Na of Gaoliang to command the northern route armies against him.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei ruler sent Prince Ren of Yongchang and Prince Na of Gaoliang to command the northern route armies against him.

sentences.zh: 檀和之等拔區粟，斬范扶龍，乘勝入象浦；

translations.literal: Tan Hezhi and others took Qu Su, beheaded Fan Fulong, and pressing their victory entered Xiang Ford;
translations.idiomatic: Tan Hezhi and others took Qu Su, beheaded Fan Fulong, and pressing their victory entered Xiang Ford;

sentences.zh: 林邑王陽邁傾國來戰，以具裝被象，前後無際。

translations.literal: King Yang Mai of Linyi came out with the whole state to fight, armored elephants front and rear without end.
translations.idiomatic: King Yang Mai of Linyi came out with the whole state to fight, armored elephants stretching front and rear without end.

sentences.zh: 宗愨曰：「吾聞外國有師子，威服百獸。」

translations.literal: Zong Que said, "I have heard that in foreign lands there are lions that by their majesty subdue all beasts."
translations.idiomatic: Zong Que said, "I have heard that in foreign lands there are lions that by their majesty subdue all beasts."

sentences.zh: 乃制其形，與象相拒，像果驚走，林邑兵大敗。

translations.literal: He then made their likenesses to confront the elephants; the elephants indeed fled in alarm and the Linyi army was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: He then made their likenesses to confront the elephants; the elephants fled in alarm and the Linyi army was routed.

sentences.zh: 和之遂克林邑，陽邁父子挺身走。

translations.literal: Hezhi then took Linyi and Yang Mai and his son fled for their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhi then took Linyi and Yang Mai and his son fled for their lives.

sentences.zh: 所獲未名之寶，不可勝計，宗愨一無所取，還家之日，衣櫛蕭然。

translations.literal: The unnamed treasures taken were beyond counting; Zong Que took nothing at all, and on the day he returned home his clothes and comb-case were bare.
translations.idiomatic: The unnamed treasures taken were beyond counting; Zong Que took nothing, and on the day he returned home his clothes and comb-case were bare.

sentences.zh: 六月，癸未朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on the guiwei new moon, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the guiwei new moon, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 甲申，魏發冀、相、定三州兵二萬人屯長安南山諸谷，以備蓋吳竄逸。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Northern Wei mobilized twenty thousand troops from the three provinces of Ji, Xiang, and Ding to encamp in the valleys of the southern mountains of Chang'an to guard against Gai Wu's escape.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, Northern Wei mobilized twenty thousand troops from Ji, Xiang, and Ding to encamp in the valleys south of Chang'an to guard against Gai Wu's escape.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，又發司、幽、定、冀四州十萬人築畿上塞圍，起上谷，西至河，廣縱千里。

translations.literal: On bingxu, they also mobilized one hundred thousand men from the four provinces of Si, You, Ding, and Ji to build the capital frontier barrier wall, starting at Shanggu, west to the river, a thousand li in breadth and length.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, they also mobilized one hundred thousand men from Si, You, Ding, and Ji to build the capital frontier barrier wall from Shanggu west to the river, a thousand li in breadth and length.

sentences.zh: 帝築北堤，立玄武湖，築景陽山於華林園。

translations.literal: The emperor built the northern embankment, established Xuanwu Lake, and built Jingyang Mountain in Hualin Park.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor built the northern embankment, established Xuanwu Lake, and built Jingyang Mountain in Hualin Park.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，辛未，以散騎常侍杜坦為青州刺史。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, on xinwei: Attendant Cavalier Du Tan was made governor of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on xinwei, Attendant Cavalier Du Tan was made governor of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 坦，驥之兄也。

translations.literal: Tan was Ji's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Tan was Ji's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 初，杜預之子耽，避晉亂，居河西，仁張氏。

translations.literal: Earlier, Du Yu's son Dan, fleeing the chaos of Jin, lived west of the river and married into the Zhang clan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Du Yu's son Dan, fleeing Jin's chaos, lived west of the river and married into the Zhang clan.

sentences.zh: 前秦克涼州，子孫始還關中。

translations.literal: When Former Qin took Liangzhou, the descendants first returned to Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Former Qin took Liangzhou, the descendants first returned to Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 高祖滅後秦，坦兄弟從高祖過江。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao destroyed Later Qin, Tan and his brothers followed Emperor Gao across the river.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao destroyed Later Qin, Tan and his brothers followed him across the river.

sentences.zh: 時江東王、謝諸族方盛，北人晚渡者，朝廷番以傖荒遇之，雖復人才可施，皆不得踐清塗。

translations.literal: At the time the Wang and Xie clans east of the Yangtze were flourishing; northerners who crossed late were repeatedly treated by the court as crude barbarians, and though talented could not tread the clear path of office.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Wang and Xie clans east of the Yangtze were flourishing; northerners who crossed late were repeatedly treated as crude outsiders, and though talented could not tread the path of office.

sentences.zh: 上嘗與坦論金日磾，曰：「恨今無復此輩人！」

translations.literal: The emperor once discussed Jin Midi with Tan and said, "I regret there are no longer men like this!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once discussed Jin Midi with Tan and said, "I regret there are no longer men like this!"

sentences.zh: 坦曰：「日磾假生今世，養馬不暇，豈辦見知！」

translations.literal: Tan said, "If Midi were born in this age, he would have no time beyond raising horses—how could he win recognition!"
translations.idiomatic: Tan said, "If Midi were born today, he would have no time beyond raising horses—how could he win recognition!"

sentences.zh: 上變色曰：「卿何量朝廷之薄也！」

translations.literal: The emperor changed color and said, "How you underestimate the court's generosity!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flushed and said, "How you underestimate the court's generosity!"

sentences.zh: 坦曰：「請以臣言之：臣本中華高族，晉氏喪亂，播遷涼土，世業相承，不殞其舊；

translations.literal: Tan said, "Let me speak of myself: I am originally of a lofty clan of the Central States; when Jin fell into chaos we were scattered to Liang lands, our hereditary estate passed down without losing its old standing;
translations.idiomatic: Tan said, "Let me speak of myself: I am originally of a lofty clan of the Central States; when Jin fell into chaos we were scattered to Liang lands, our hereditary estate passed down without losing its standing;

sentences.zh: 直以南度不早，便以荒傖賜隔。

translations.literal: simply because we crossed south not early enough, we are set apart as crude barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: simply because we crossed south not early enough, we are set apart as crude outsiders.

sentences.zh: 日磾，胡人，身為牧圉，乃超登內侍，齒列名賢。

translations.literal: Midi was a barbarian, a horse-herd by station, yet he rose straight to palace attendance and stood among famed worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Midi was a barbarian, a horse-herd by station, yet he rose straight to palace attendance and stood among famed worthies.

sentences.zh: 聖朝雖復拔才，臣恐未必能也。」

translations.literal: Though the sage court again selects talent, your servant fears it may not be possible."
translations.idiomatic: Though the sage court selects talent, I fear it may not be possible."

sentences.zh: 上默然。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was silent.

sentences.zh: 八月，魏高涼王那等破蓋吳，獲其二叔；

translations.literal: Eighth month: Northern Wei's Prince Na of Gaoliang and others broke Gai Wu and captured his two uncles;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Northern Wei's Prince Na of Gaoliang and others broke Gai Wu and captured his two uncles;

sentences.zh: 諸將欲送詣平城，長安鎮將陸俟曰：「長安險固，風俗豪忮，平時猶不可忽，況承荒亂之餘乎！

translations.literal: the generals wished to send them to Pingcheng; Garrison Commander of Chang'an Lu Si said, "Chang'an is strong and secure, its customs proud and contentious—even in normal times it cannot be neglected, how much less after the aftermath of chaos!
translations.idiomatic: the generals wished to send them to Pingcheng; Garrison Commander of Chang'an Lu Si said, "Chang'an is strong and secure, its customs proud and contentious—even in normal times it cannot be neglected, how much less after chaos!

sentences.zh: 今不斬吳，則長安之變未已也。

translations.literal: If Wu is not beheaded now, Chang'an's troubles will not cease.
translations.idiomatic: If Wu is not beheaded now, Chang'an's troubles will not cease.

sentences.zh: 吳一身潛竄，非其親信，誰能獲之！

translations.literal: Wu alone is in hiding—who but his close followers can capture him!
translations.idiomatic: Wu alone is in hiding—who but his close followers can capture him!

sentences.zh: 若停十萬之眾以追一人，又非長策。

translations.literal: To halt one hundred thousand men to pursue one person is again no long-term plan.
translations.idiomatic: To halt one hundred thousand men to pursue one person is again no long-term plan.

sentences.zh: 不如私許吳叔，免其妻子，使自追吳，擒之必矣。」

translations.literal: Better to secretly promise Wu's uncles, spare their wives and children, and have them pursue Wu themselves—capture is certain."
translations.idiomatic: Better to secretly promise Wu's uncles, spare their wives and children, and have them pursue Wu themselves—capture is certain."

sentences.zh: 諸將鹹曰：「今賊黨眾已散，唯吳一身，何所能至？」

translations.literal: The generals all said, "Now the rebel band is scattered; only Wu alone—what can he accomplish?"
translations.idiomatic: The generals all said, "Now the rebel band is scattered; only Wu alone—what can he accomplish?"

sentences.zh: 俟曰：「諸君不見毒蛇乎！

translations.literal: Si said, "Do you not see the poisonous snake!
translations.idiomatic: Si said, "Have you never seen a poisonous snake!

sentences.zh: 不斷其首，猶能為害。

translations.literal: If you do not cut off its head, it can still do harm.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not cut off its head, it can still do harm.

sentences.zh: 吳天性凶狡，今若得脫，必自稱王者不死，以惑愚民，為患愈大。」

translations.literal: Wu is by nature fierce and cunning; if he escapes now he will surely declare himself a king who cannot die, to delude the foolish people—the harm will be greater."
translations.idiomatic: Wu is by nature fierce and cunning; if he escapes now he will declare himself a king who cannot die, to delude the people—the harm will be greater."

sentences.zh: 諸將曰：「公言是也。

translations.literal: The generals said, "Your words are right.
translations.idiomatic: The generals said, "You are right.

sentences.zh: 但得賊不殺，而更遣之，若遂往不返，將何以任其罪？」

translations.literal: But if we do not kill the captives and instead send them off, if they go and do not return, how shall we bear the blame?"
translations.idiomatic: But if we do not kill the captives and instead send them off, if they go and do not return, how shall we bear the blame?"

sentences.zh: 俟曰：「此罪我為諸君任之。」

translations.literal: Si said, "For this crime I will bear responsibility for you all."
translations.idiomatic: Si said, "For this I will bear responsibility for you all."

sentences.zh: 高涼王那亦以俟計為然，遂赦二叔，與刻期而遣之。

translations.literal: Prince Na of Gaoliang also thought Si's plan correct, and so pardoned the two uncles and sent them off with a fixed deadline.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Na of Gaoliang also agreed with Si's plan, pardoned the two uncles, and sent them off with a fixed deadline.

sentences.zh: 及期，吳叔不至，諸將皆咎俟，俟曰：「彼伺之未得其便耳，必不負也。」

translations.literal: When the deadline came the uncles did not arrive; the generals all blamed Si, and Si said, "They are watching and have not yet found their opportunity—they will not fail us."
translations.idiomatic: When the deadline came the uncles did not arrive; the generals all blamed Si, and Si said, "They are watching and have not yet found their opportunity—they will not fail us."

sentences.zh: 後數日，吳叔果以吳首來；

translations.literal: Several days later the uncles indeed came with Wu's head;
translations.idiomatic: Several days later the uncles indeed came with Wu's head;

sentences.zh: 傳詣平城。

translations.literal: it was sent on to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: it was sent on to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 永昌王仁等討吳餘黨白廣平、路那羅等，悉平之。

translations.literal: Prince Ren of Yongchang and others campaigned against Wu's remaining followers Bai Guang and Lu Naluo and pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ren of Yongchang and others campaigned against Wu's remaining followers Bai Guang and Lu Naluo and pacified them all.

sentences.zh: 以陸俟為內都大官。

translations.literal: Lu Si was made Chief Palace Provisioner of the Inner Court.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Si was made Chief Palace Provisioner of the Inner Court.

sentences.zh: 會安定盧水胡劉超等聚眾萬餘人反，魏主以俟威恩著於關中，復加俟都督秦、雍二州諸軍事，鎮長安。

translations.literal: When Liu Chao of the Lu River Hu of Anding and others gathered more than ten thousand followers and rebelled, the Northern Wei ruler, because Si's authority and kindness were renowned in Guanzhong, again added to him command of military affairs for the two provinces of Qin and Yong and stationed him to guard Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Chao of the Lu River Hu of Anding and others gathered more than ten thousand followers and rebelled, the Northern Wei ruler, because Si's authority and kindness were renowned in Guanzhong, again made him commander of Qin and Yong and stationed him at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 謂俟曰：「關中奉化日淺，恩信未洽，吏民數為逆亂。

translations.literal: He said to Si, "Guanzhong has accepted transformation only recently; grace and trust are not yet settled, and officials and people have repeatedly rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: He said to Si, "Guanzhong has accepted transformation only recently; grace and trust are not yet settled, and officials and people have repeatedly rebelled.

sentences.zh: 今朕以重兵授卿，則超等必同心協力，據險拒守，未易攻也；

translations.literal: If I now give you a heavy force, Chao and the others will surely unite in heart and strength, hold the passes and resist—not easy to attack;
translations.idiomatic: If I now give you a heavy force, Chao and the others will unite, hold the passes and resist—not easy to attack;

sentences.zh: 若兵少，則不能制賊，卿當自以方略取之。」

translations.literal: if the force is small you cannot control the rebels—you must take them by your own stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: if the force is small you cannot control the rebels—you must take them by your own stratagem."

sentences.zh: 俟乃單馬之鎮。

translations.literal: Si then went to his post alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Si then went to his post alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 超等聞之，大喜，以俟為無能為也。

translations.literal: Chao and the others heard and were greatly pleased, thinking Si could do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Chao and the others heard and were greatly pleased, thinking Si could do nothing.

sentences.zh: 俟既至，諭以成敗，誘納超女，與為姻戚以招之；

translations.literal: When Si arrived he explained success and failure, offered marriage to Chao's daughter, and made kinship to win him over;
translations.idiomatic: When Si arrived he explained success and failure, offered marriage to Chao's daughter, and made kinship to win him over;

sentences.zh: 超自恃其眾，猶無降意。

translations.literal: Chao, relying on his numbers, still had no thought of surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Chao, relying on his numbers, still had no thought of surrender.

sentences.zh: 俟乃帥其帳下親往見超，超使人逆謂俟曰：「從者過三百人，當以弓馬相待；

translations.literal: Si then led his personal followers to visit Chao in person; Chao sent someone ahead to tell Si, "If your followers exceed three hundred, we shall meet you with bow and horse;
translations.idiomatic: Si then led his personal followers to visit Chao; Chao sent word to Si, "If your followers exceed three hundred, we shall meet you with bow and horse;

sentences.zh: 不及三百人，當以酒食相供。」

translations.literal: if fewer than three hundred, we shall supply wine and food."
translations.idiomatic: if fewer than three hundred, we shall supply wine and food."

sentences.zh: 俟乃將二百騎詣超。

translations.literal: Si then took two hundred cavalry to Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Si then took two hundred cavalry to Chao.

sentences.zh: 超設備甚嚴，俟縱酒盡醉而還。

translations.literal: Chao made preparations very strict; Si drank freely until thoroughly drunk and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Chao made strict preparations; Si drank freely until thoroughly drunk and returned.

sentences.zh: 頃之，俟復選敢死士五百人出獵，因詣超營，約曰：「發機當以醉為限。」

translations.literal: Before long Si again selected five hundred dare-to-die men to go hunting and thereby visited Chao's camp, agreeing, "The signal to strike shall be when drunk."
translations.idiomatic: Before long Si again selected five hundred dare-to-die men to go hunting and visited Chao's camp, agreeing, "The signal to strike shall be when drunk."

sentences.zh: 既飲，俟陽醉，上馬大呼，手斬超首；

translations.literal: After drinking, Si feigned drunkenness, mounted his horse and shouted loudly, and with his own hand beheaded Chao;
translations.idiomatic: After drinking, Si feigned drunkenness, mounted his horse and shouted, and with his own hand beheaded Chao;

sentences.zh: 士卒應聲縱擊，殺傷千數，遂平之。

translations.literal: soldiers responded and struck; more than a thousand were killed and wounded, and it was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: soldiers responded and struck; more than a thousand were killed and wounded, and it was pacified.

sentences.zh: 魏主征俟還，為外都大官。

translations.literal: The Northern Wei ruler summoned Si back and made him Chief Palace Provisioner of the Outer Court.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei ruler summoned Si back and made him Chief Palace Provisioner of the Outer Court.

sentences.zh: 是歲，吐谷渾復還舊土。

translations.literal: That year, Tuyuhun returned to their former lands.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Tuyuhun returned to their former lands.
